research.quote: Abu Dhabi’s first Health Information Exchange (HIE) platform, Malaffi, has announced that all public and private hospitals in the Emirate are now connected to the platform.
research.source: Malaffi (Abu Dhabi Health Information Exchange, operated by Abu Dhabi Health Data Services under the Department of Health Abu Dhabi): press release 'All of Abu Dhabi’s hospitals connect to health information exchange Malaffi'
research.notes: English source, no translation needed. Kind of private: privately owned hospitals and clinics in Abu Dhabi and Dubai, whether insurer-paid or self-pay; the UAE system is insurance-based and the HIE obligation attaches to the facility licence, not to the payer. Write, not read: Malaffi and NABIDH ingest clinical data from connected facilities (the same page: access to patient information 'captured from 98% patient episodes' across 1,539 facilities). RULE IN FORCE, Abu Dhabi: DOH Standard on Patient Healthcare Data Privacy (DOH/SD/SS/PHDP/0.9, effective 16 Sep 2020), https://staticcdn.malaffi.ae/wpblobe9e5523f25/2021/02/2020-09-15-DOH-Standard-on-Patient-Healthcare-Data-Privacy-for-publication-2.pdf, clause 6.4: 'Entities shall exchange information on Abu Dhabi Health Information Exchange, Malaffi, in accordance with DOH’s Chairman Resolution no. 90, 2018, the rules, circulars, policies and agreements in implementation thereof.' with scope 2.1.1 'All categories of health care entities regulated by DOH in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi.' RULE IN FORCE, Dubai: DHA External Circular # 0954 (CIR-2025-00000101, 26 May 2025), addressed 'To: All Health Professionals & Health Facilities under the jurisdiction of Dubai Heath Authority –Dubai', supporting document titled 'Health Facilities Compulsory to Integrate with NABIDH', https://services.dha.gov.ae/sheryan/wps/portal/home/circular-details?circularRefNo=CIR-2025-00000101&isPublicCircular=1&fromHome=true ; DHA Standards for Health Information Consent and Access Control (DHA/HISHD/ST-09, effective 02/04/2025) define NABIDH as the platform 'that connects public and private healthcare facilities in Dubai to securely exchange trusted health information'. Sub-national: three exchanges (Malaffi Abu Dhabi, NABIDH Dubai, Riayati federal/northern emirates) linked since 2023 per the existing country file; no source opened names a gap for private providers in any emirate. No gap, no future deadline, rule in force covers all licensed facilities, so connected. Existing country file class: unknown (silent on private); this research gives connected.

research.quote: This Act was passed on 14 February 2025 to mandate that key health information - starting with pathology and diagnostic imaging reports - be automatically shared to My Health Record. The range of clinical documents will be added incrementally over time.
research.source: Victorian Department of Health, My Health Record for Victorian Health Services
research.notes: English, no translation needed. The quote names the staged scope, not private providers; the private-provider gap rests on the Bills Digest sentences below. Law in force with a staged scope: the Health Legislation Amendment (Modernising My Health Record; Sharing by Default) Act 2025 (assent 14 February 2025) and the My Health Record (Share by Default) Rules, commencing 1 July 2026, require the authors of pathology and diagnostic imaging reports to upload them to My Health Record. The lever is Medicare: Part 2 of the Act amends the Health Insurance Act so that Medicare benefits are not payable for prescribed services unless the report is shared, so it reaches Medicare-billed services, which include the private pathology businesses the digest names ("Australian Pathology (representing private pathology businesses)"), and which the brief treats as a grey zone rather than private. Private hospitals and private specialists are not yet required to upload. Second source, Parliamentary Library Bills Digest No. 42, 2024-25 (30 January 2025), https://www.aph.gov.au/Parliamentary_Business/Bills_Legislation/bd/bd2425/25bd042 : "Providers within the pathology and diagnostic imaging sectors are intended to be the first required to share test results to the My Health Record system."; "Authorised healthcare providers can upload and view a patient's health information, however, it is currently voluntary for providers to upload information."; and, quoting the Impact Analysis, "some large private providers have indicated that meeting new share by default requirements for uploading reports to My Health Record would not become their standard practice until a legal requirement to do so is established." Commencement confirmed by Hall & Wilcox, 13 April 2026 (law firm, secondary): "The new My Health Record (Share by Default) Rules, commencing on 1 July 2026 specify: which healthcare providers must upload information – starting with pathology and imaging services". WRITE: private hospitals and specialists may upload discharge summaries and specialist letters, but voluntarily. The ADHA (digitalhealth.gov.au) and health.gov.au reset every connection from this environment, so the operator's participation statistics for private hospitals and specialists were not verified. Existing class in the country file: unknown. This changes it to partial.

research.quote: Alle Belgische ziekenhuizen en klinische labo’s zijn aangesloten op een ziekenhuisnetwerk.
research.source: Gegevensbeschermingsautoriteit (Belgian Data Protection Authority), Advies nr. 127/2023 van 8 september 2023 (on the draft law on the hubs-metahub system)
research.notes: Definition first: under the brief, a privately owned provider that bills the public plan is not 'private'. In Belgium nearly every doctor is a self-employed fee-for-service practitioner billing INAMI/RIZIV (conventionné or non-conventionné, both reimbursed), and most hospitals are privately owned non-profits financed by INAMI (hospital ownership not sourced in this pass). So the brief's 'private' sector in Belgium is care paid wholly outside INAMI (e.g. aesthetic clinics, non-reimbursed care). No public source found that says anything about whether such providers publish to the hubs, Vitalink, Réseau Santé Wallon, Abrumet/Brusafe or CoZo, so the class is unknown. Grey-zone evidence recorded for the file, write side: (1) GBA advice 127/2023, p. on the hubs-metahub system: 'Alle Belgische ziekenhuizen en klinische labo's zijn aangesloten op een ziekenhuisnetwerk.' ('All Belgian hospitals and clinical laboratories are connected to a hospital network', i.e. one of the four hubs that publish documents to the eHealth metahub); these hospitals include the privately owned INAMI-financed ones. (2) GP summaries (Sumehr) are published by incentive, not by obligation: RIZIV, 'Uitleg bij de voorwaarden voor de geïntegreerde praktijkpremie huisartsgeneeskunde', https://www.riziv.fgov.be/nl/professionals/individuele-zorgverleners/artsen/financiele-tegemoetkomingen/geintegreerde-praktijkpremie/uitleg-bij-de-voorwaarden-voor-de-geintegreerde-praktijkpremie-huisartsgeneeskunde (undated page, premium years 2025 and 2026): 'De verhouding tussen het totaal aantal verschillende patiënten waarvoor u uiterlijk op 31 december 2025 een SUMEHR hebt opgeladen via de digitale platformen Vitalink, RSW of Abrumet en het aantal patiënten waarvoor u voor 2025 een GMD-honorarium heeft ontvangen, bedraagt minstens 60%.' ('The ratio between the total number of distinct patients for whom you uploaded a SUMEHR via Vitalink, RSW or Abrumet by 31 December 2025 and the number of patients for whom you received a GMD fee for 2025 is at least 60%'), a premium condition tied to INAMI fees. Read side: eHealth-platform, 'Verwijzingsrepertorium (Metahub)', https://www.ehealth.fgov.be/ehealthplatform/nl/service-verwijzingsrepertorium-metahub (undated): 'Deze diensten zijn, naargelang het geval, toegankelijk voor hubs, individuele zorgverleners, bepaalde zorginstellingen zoals ziekenhuizen of apotheken en ook voor patiënten.' ('These services are, as the case may be, accessible to hubs, individual care providers, certain care institutions such as hospitals or pharmacies, and also to patients') and 'De webservice Metahub is enkel toegankelijk voor de hubs die erkend zijn door het eHealth-platform en dient dus geïntegreerd te worden in de informatica-oplossing van de hub.' ('The Metahub web service is accessible only to hubs recognised by the eHealth platform'). If the owner accepts the grey zone as 'private', the INAMI-financed private hospitals are connected (GBA sentence) and GPs are incentivised, which would read as connected for hospitals; for the brief's strict definition it stays unknown. Agrees with the existing country-file class (unknown, silent).

research.quote: Estamos criando um vaso comunicante, digamos assim, entre os dois, para que os dados privados venham para a RNDS.
research.source: Futuro da Saúde, interview with Ana Estela Haddad, Secretária de Informação e Saúde Digital (SEIDIGI), Ministério da Saúde: 'Projeto de lei é virada de chave para a interoperabilidade público-privada'
research.notes: Translation: 'We are creating a communicating vessel, so to speak, between the two [public and private], so that private data comes to the RNDS.' Next sentence on the same page: 'Não é o todo, vem aquilo que é importante para a continuidade do atendimento clínico, para as políticas públicas e para vigilância em saúde.' ('It is not everything; what comes is what matters for continuity of clinical care, public policy and health surveillance.') Same page, on the decree: 'O projeto de lei avança em questões que não estavam ainda regulamentadas no decreto da RNDS, principalmente na relação público-privada e no modelo de governança.' ('The bill advances on matters not yet regulated in the RNDS decree, chiefly the public-private relationship and the governance model.') WRITE direction: 'dados privados venham para a RNDS' is private providers feeding the national record (RNDS, read by citizens in Meu SUS Digital). The ministry's own secretary says that channel is being built and is partial, so partial. Rule in force: Decreto nº 12.560, de 23 de julho de 2025, Art. 4º, https://www.planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2023-2026/2025/decreto/d12560.htm : 'O envio dos dados referidos no art. 3º, caput, para a RNDS será feito por estabelecimentos públicos e privados, conforme modelos informacionais e computacionais padronizados e definidos na forma do Capítulo III' ('Sending of the data ... to the RNDS shall be done by public and private establishments, according to standardised information and computational models defined under Chapter III'); it sets no deadline for private establishments and Art. 19 leaves implementation to future ministry norms and manuals. Measured share (second source): Cetic.br/NIC.br, Pesquisa TIC Saúde 2025 (published São Paulo 2026, PDF dated 12 May 2026), https://cetic.br/media/docs/publicacoes/2/pt-br/20260512115627/TIC_SAUDE_2025_PT_livro.pdf , p. 65: 'Os resultados da TIC Saúde 2025 indicam que 44% dos estabelecimentos de saúde que utilizaram a Internet estão integrados à RNDS. A integração é mais comum nas UBS (72%) e nos estabelecimentos públicos (64%) (Gráfico 6).' ('44% of health establishments that used the Internet are integrated to the RNDS; integration is most common in basic health units (72%) and public establishments (64%).') Gráfico 6 on the same page shows Privado 27%. 'Integrado' is self-reported and not defined as write vs read. EXCLUDED as a private-provider link per brief: the ANS (health-plan regulator) feed to RNDS. Haddad on the same page: 'É fato que não chegam dados clínicos, mas chegam registros de atendimento.' ('Clinical data do not arrive; encounter records do.') Mobile Time, 28 Jan 2026, https://www.mobiletime.com.br/noticias/28/01/2026/saude-sus-dados-enviados/ : '2 bilhões de dados foram enviados das empresas de saúde particular reguladas pela Agência Nacional de Saúde Suplementar (ANS) para a Rede Nacional de Saúde Digital (RNDS) do SUS' and 'a troca de dados é apenas da ANS para o RNDS'. That is an insurer/TISS claims link, operadoras not providers, and covers only people with private plans; it does not count here. Draft law: the substitutivo to PL 5875/2013 (reported 12 May 2026) would make interoperability mandatory for public and private systems; not in force, zero weight. Which kind of private: Brazil's private providers serve both health-plan (saúde suplementar) and out-of-pocket patients; private labs already send some notifiable-disease results to RNDS (Haddad on the same page: 'Antes tínhamos os de Covid e monkeypox', with work under way to add 40 agravos), a narrow write; the 2020 Covid-lab portaria is referenced in secondary sources only and was not opened. Against the country file: AGREES (partial, 'Private sector integration and small hospitals still lag').

recordSplit.quote: Diagnostic imaging reports from most private clinics will not be available in Health Gateway as they currently are not available to our provincial repository.
recordSplit.note: The file documents fragmentation across provinces and practices, not a public/private split.

research.quote: Diagnostic imaging reports from most private clinics will not be available in Health Gateway as they currently are not available to our provincial repository.
research.source: British Columbia Ministry of Health, Digital Health Initiative: Health Gateway 'Diagnostic Imaging Reports' frequently asked questions
research.notes:
NATIONAL READING: partial. Canada has no national EHR; the shared record is provincial. In each of the four provinces examined (ON, BC, AB, QC) some private providers write to the provincial record (community pharmacies regardless of payer in BC and QC; private labs and private imaging labs by law in QC; licensed Integrated Community Health Services Centres under a Jan 2025 regulation in ON; independent radiology clinics listed as Netcare contributors in AB) while other private care does not reach it (most private imaging clinics in BC; non-MSP-billed visits in BC; private physician offices and private surgical centres in QC, which may only read; Alberta community clinics joining 'as they are ready' under a permissive statute). No province's source says private-pay care as such is written, and none says it is wholly excluded, so the class is partial, not split. The national quote is the BC Ministry of Health sentence because it is the clearest ministry statement of a write-side gap that names private clinics. WRITE vs READ: every provincial viewer (ConnectingOntario, CareConnect, Alberta Netcare Portal, DSQ visualiseur) is a read tool; private clinicians in all four provinces can get read access, which does not count. Patient portals (Health Gateway, MyHealth Records, Carnet sante Quebec) are read-only and show only what the repositories hold. KIND OF PRIVATE: Canadian 'private clinics' are mostly privately owned and mixed-payer (public plan plus uninsured, third-party or out-of-pocket). Where a rule attaches to the facility or custodian (QC imaging labs, ON ICHSCs, BC pharmacies) a private-pay encounter at that facility would flow too, but no source states that step for private-pay imaging or surgery; it is unverified, not confirmed. Private-pay-only providers (private virtual care, membership clinics, non-participating physicians) are covered by no rule found. 

--- BRITISH COLUMBIA (reading: partial) --- Source 1 (national quote): BC Ministry of Health, Digital Health Initiative, 'Diagnostic Imaging Reports' Health Gateway FAQ, last updated 2024-03-12, https://www2.gov.bc.ca/assets/gov/health/accessing-health-care/health-gateway/health-gateway-resources/health_gateway_diagnostic_imaging_faqs.pdf : 'Diagnostic imaging reports from most private clinics will not be available in Health Gateway as they currently are not available to our provincial repository.' The same PDF lists 'Health visits billed to BC MSP (date, location, visit type and provider name)'. Source 2: Government of BC, 'Access your health records with Health Gateway', undated (read 2026-10-01), https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/health/managing-your-health/health-gateway : 'Private imaging facility reports are not included.' and 'Any health visits billed to the BC Medical Services Plan (MSP) in the past 7 years are shown.' Guide page https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/health/managing-your-health/health-gateway/guide/healthrecords : 'You can not currently get: Images Reports from procedures performed before September 2023 Reports from private imaging facilities Reports for dependents aged 11 or younger'. Source 3 (pharmacy, connected regardless of payer): BC Ministry of Health, PharmaNet Conformance Standards Volume 4C, v3.7, 2026-02-20, https://www2.gov.bc.ca/assets/gov/health/practitioner-pro/software-development-guidelines/conformance-standards/vol-4c-app-rules-pnet.pdf , rule PNetTx20.2: 'Transmit all prescriptions dispensed regardless of payer.' PharmaCare Policy Manual s. 2.3 (2025-03-28) says prescriptions dispensed in community pharmacies 'must be entered on PharmaNet, whether or not: The patient is covered by PharmaCare'. Source 4 (read side): my.careconnect.ca (note dated 2023-01-16): 'CareConnect is British Columbia's secure, view-only Electronic Health Record (EHR)'; it offers 'clinical documents from both non health authority and health authority sources', so some non-health-authority (community or private) labs and documents do feed it; which private providers is not listed. 

--- ONTARIO (reading: partial; rule in force with 'as requested' scope) --- Source 1: O. Reg. 493/24, s. 1 (in force 2025-01-01), substituting s. 18.1.3 (1) of O. Reg. 329/04 under PHIPA. The e-Laws page https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/r24493 needs JavaScript; the text is reproduced on isdco.ca (ISDCO, an Ontario organisation; its page says 'This information was provided by the Digital Health Program Branch of the Ministry of Health'), 2025-01-13, https://www.isdco.ca/news/ishscs-to-comply-contribute-certain-personal-health-info : '(1) The classes of health information custodians or specific health information custodians listed in subsection (1.1) shall provide to the Agency for the electronic health record personal health information contained in a digital health asset, (a) as requested by the Agency; and (b) in accordance with the interoperability specifications of the Agency.' and '(1.1) The classes of health information custodians or specific health information custodians referred to in subsection (1) are every person who operates one of the following: 1. A hospital within the meaning of the Public Hospitals Act. 2. A pharmacy for which a certificate of accreditation of the community pharmacy class has been issued under the Drug and Pharmacies Regulation Act. 3. An integrated community health services centre within the meaning of the Integrated Community Health Services Centres Act, 2023.' ISDCO adds that the duty bites 'once published' (the specifications). Source 2 (primary, proposal stage): Ontario Gazette vol. 157 issue 21, 2024-05-25, Notice of Minister of Health, https://www.ontario.ca/document/ontario-gazette-volume-157-issue-21-may-25-2024/government-notices-other : 'In addition to the existing requirement for operators of public hospitals, the proposed amendments would, if approved, require operators of accredited community pharmacies and integrated community health services centres to contribute certain personal health information to the EHR as requested by OH and in accordance with OH's interoperability specifications.' Ontario Hospital Association, 'Legal and Regulatory Highlights for Hospitals', January 2025: 'To address data gaps in the EHR, the new amendments mandate accredited community pharmacies and integrated community health services centres to also contribute PHI to the EHR.' Source 3 (gap, imaging): Ontario Health / eHealth Ontario, 'DI CS Data Summary', undated, https://ehealthontario.on.ca/connectingontario-data-summary/DICS_data_summary.html : 'The DI CS contains reports and images submitted by hospitals and independent health facilities to the province's three regional Diagnostic Imaging Repositories (DI-rs).' and 'Note: Data made accessible through the Provincial Clinical Viewers is limited to information contributed to Ontario Health by participating Health Information Custodians.' Its contributors list (DI Data Contributors v14, March 2021, https://ehealthontario.on.ca/files/public/support/DICS_DataContributors_EN.pdf) lists 17 independent health facilities against 184 hospital rows (rows with a contribution date, counted from the PDF) and says 'Contributions from additional IHF's will be updated as the information becomes available'. Source 4 (audit): Auditor General of Ontario, 2018 Annual Report vol. 2, s. 1.03 'Electronic Health Records' Implementation Status' follow-up, https://www.auditor.on.ca/en/content/annualreports/arreports/en18/v2_103en18.pdf : 'We found in 2016 that many independent health facilities were not able to provide diagnostic images, such as x-rays, MRIs, CT scans and mammograms, to the repository because they did not use digital equipment.' and 'The five-year target for the period 2016/17 to 2020/21 is to have 80%–90% of independent health facilities contributing to the diagnostic imaging repositories.' Source 5 (licensing): Ministry of Health, Call for Applications Guidelines, MRI and CT services (ICHSCs), 2024-06-03, https://www.ontario.ca/files/2024-05/moh-mri-ct-call-for-application-guidelines-en-2024-06-03.pdf : applicants must 'Confirm understanding that future licensing requirements can include digital connectivity and reporting requirements, such as participation in the centralized waitlist management program, the regional central intake program, the provincial electronic health record, etc.' It defines 'Uninsured Services: means services that are not insured under OHIP' and says 'Patients may pay fees for these services directly.' Kind of private: ICHSCs (formerly Independent Health Facilities) are privately operated, mainly OHIP-funded, with some uninsured or private-pay services; the duty attaches to the operator, not the payer, but Ontario Health's requests and specifications were not found, so coverage of private-pay encounters is unverified. 

--- ALBERTA (reading: partial; permissive statute, independent DI clinics feed) --- Source 1: Alberta Netcare (Government of Alberta operator site), home page, copyright 2026, https://www.albertanetcare.ca/ : 'Each health care location submits key patient health information to Alberta Netcare.' Source 2: Alberta Netcare Portal Data Availability table, 'As of 1-Jan-2026', https://www.albertanetcare.ca/documents/ANP_Data_Availability_Table_Summary.pdf : lists 'DI Text Reports - Independent Clinics' and PACS image feeds from private radiology operators including 'Mayfair Diagnostics. Riley Park, Mayfair Place, Southcentre, Sunpark', 'Canada Diagnostic Centres (CDC) Savanna' and 'Sunridge Diagnostic Imaging - Calgary'; the community clinics row (CII) reads 'EMR clinic locations onboarded as they are ready' (table cell); for immunization: 'As of January 1, 2021 all vaccine providers are submitting both provincially funded and privately purchased immunization information to Alberta Health'. Source 3 (law): Health Information Act, RSA 2000 c H-5, current as of 2026-07-02, https://kings-printer.alberta.ca/documents/Acts/H05.pdf , s. 56.31: 'An authorized custodian may make the health information prescribed in the regulations that is in its custody or under its control accessible via the Alberta EHR in accordance with the regulations.' s. 56.3(1): a professional body 'may in writing direct' a regulated provider to make information accessible, and s. 56.3(3.1): 'A regulated health services provider must comply with a direction made under subsection (1) or (2).' So the write duty exists only on direction; no general direction covering private clinics was found. The Act's custodian definition does not turn on payer. Source 4 (private operator): Mayfair Diagnostics (private radiology group performing 'private pay MRIs in Calgary since 1999'), 'How do I get a private MRI?', 2022-08-01, https://www.radiology.ca/article/how-do-i-get-private-mri/ : 'Your images will be uploaded to a provincial picture archiving and communication system (PACS)'; and 'Questions about your medical imaging results', 2022-02-08, https://www.radiology.ca/article/questions-about-your-medical-imaging-results/ : 'In Alberta, images are uploaded to Netcare, Alberta's electronic health record system.' Facility-level evidence that private-pay imaging reaches Netcare; no sentence states the payer step explicitly. Source 5: College of Physicians and Surgeons of Alberta, Council agenda, June 2025, https://cpsa.ca/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/Council-Agenda-Dossier-Items.pdf : accreditation program work includes 'expanded data integration into Netcare among accredited facilities' (non-hospital surgical and diagnostic facilities), so integration is not complete. Chartered surgical facilities: no source found on whether operative reports reach Netcare; unverified. 

--- QUEBEC (reading: partial; law feeds pharmacies, labs and imaging labs including private, but private physician offices and private surgical centres only read) --- Source 1 (law in force): Loi concernant le partage de certains renseignements de santé, RLRQ c. P-9.0001, à jour au 10 juin 2026, https://www.legisquebec.gouv.qc.ca/fr/document/lc/P-9.0001 , art. 31: 'Un établissement qui exploite un centre dans lequel est formé un département clinique d’imagerie médicale de même qu’une personne ou une société qui exploite un laboratoire d’imagerie médicale générale ou un laboratoire de radiologie diagnostique spécifique à la médecine doit communiquer, le plus tôt possible, au gestionnaire opérationnel d’une banque de renseignements de santé du domaine imagerie médicale les renseignements de santé visés à l’article 33 concernant tout résultat d’examen d’imagerie médicale qu’il produit à l’égard d’une personne.' [Translation: An institution operating a centre with a clinical medical imaging department, as well as a person or company operating a general medical imaging laboratory or a diagnostic radiology laboratory, must communicate, as soon as possible, to the operational manager of the medical imaging domain health information bank the information referred to in s. 33 concerning every medical imaging result it produces for a person.] Art. 23 imposes the same duty on every community pharmacy for every medication; art. 28 on institutions and private medical biology laboratories for every lab result; art. 40 on institutions, 'cabinet privé de médecin' and 'centre médical spécialisé' only for allergies and intolerances; art. 43 on hospital centres only for the hospitalization summary. The law has no term 'non participant'; duties attach to facility type, not payer, so patient-paid imaging at a private imaging lab is covered. Source 2: Gouvernement du Québec, 'Renseignements disponibles - Dossier santé Québec', updated 2026-04-07, https://www.quebec.ca/sante/vos-informations-de-sante/dossier-sante-quebec/renseignements-disponibles : 'Domaine Imagerie médicale Renseignements disponibles : Les résultats des examens d’imagerie médicale effectués dans un établissement ou un laboratoire privé d’imagerie médicale générale ou de radiologie diagnostique spécifique à la médecine.' [Translation: Medical imaging domain, information available: results of medical imaging exams done in an institution or in a private general medical imaging or diagnostic radiology laboratory.] Also: 'Domaine Allergie et intolérance Renseignements à venir : les allergies et les intolérances.' [Allergy and intolerance domain: information to come], so the one domain private physician offices and CMS must feed is not live. Source 3: Gouvernement du Québec, 'Organismes autorisés - Dossier santé Québec', updated 2026-04-07, https://www.quebec.ca/sante/vos-informations-de-sante/dossier-sante-quebec/organismes-autorises : 'Les cabinets privés de médecins, les cabinets privés de professionnels et professionnelles et les centres médicaux spécialisés peuvent : consulter les renseignements concernant les médicaments; consulter les résultats de laboratoire; consulter les résultats d’imagerie médicale.' [Translation: Private physician offices, private professional offices and specialized medical centres may: consult medication information; consult lab results; consult imaging results.] By contrast, laboratories and imaging laboratories on the same page 'peuvent transmettre' (may transmit). Centres médicaux spécialisés are Quebec's private surgical centres, so privately paid surgery there is read-only to the DSQ. Source 4: MSSS, 'Liste des sites d’imagerie médicale branchés au Dossier santé Québec', sites connected as of 7 May 2024, published 2024-07-04, https://publications.msss.gouv.qc.ca/msss/fichiers/2024/DSQ_Imagerie_2024-06-26.pdf : 'La date entre parenthèses indique le moment du branchement au DSQ. Les examens réalisés avant cette date ne se retrouvent pas au DSQ.' [Translation: The date in parentheses is when the site connected to the DSQ. Exams done before that date are not in the DSQ.] The list mixes public hospitals and private radiology clinics (e.g. 'IRM Saguenay-Lac-St-Jean (2018-12-11)'). MSSS regulatory impact analysis, 2018 (publication 18-715-04W, https://publications.msss.gouv.qc.ca/msss/fichiers/2018/18-715-04W.pdf): 'Ce ne sont que les établissements du secteur public qui vont alimenter le domaine sommaire d’hospitalisation à l’aide du dossier clinique informatisé (DCI) Cristal-Net.' [Translation: Only public-sector institutions will feed the hospitalization summary domain, using the Cristal-Net clinical information system.] 

--- CANADA-WIDE --- Bill S-5, Connected Care for Canadians Act (LEGISinfo, https://www.parl.ca/legisinfo/en/bill/45-1/s-5): 'Latest activity First reading on Thursday, May 28, 2026 (House of Commons)'. Not in force, and it binds health IT vendors (anti data blocking), not private care providers, so it cannot move the class. CMAJ 2026;198(17):E644 environmental scan of EHR interoperability does not mention private providers. Canada Health Infoway pages speak of 'industry and private sector' as vendors, not care providers. No CIHI or federal source found on private-provider contribution. 

AGREEMENT WITH EXISTING CLASS: the country file is 'unknown' (journeyNote: 'only 35% of physicians share data outside their practice'; nothing on public vs private). The new provincial sources support moving CAN to 'partial': private pharmacies, labs and imaging labs are written in by law or practice in some provinces, while private clinics, private surgical centres and most private imaging in BC are named gaps. This does not confirm the strain hypothesis that private care splits the record wholesale; it shows a province-by-province, service-by-service split. Not found: any source on private virtual-care or membership clinics writing to a provincial record; any source on chartered surgical facilities (AB) or CMS (QC) operative reports reaching the viewer; the Quebec Carnet santé FAQ (carnetsante.gouv.qc.ca returned 403). Quotes were checked word for word against the saved page text; French quotes keep the sources' accents and typographic apostrophes.

research.quote: Für alle anderen ambulant tätigen Gesundheitsfachpersonen sowie für Patientinnen und Patienten ist die Eröffnung des EPD freiwillig.
research.source: Bundesamt für Gesundheit (BAG), 'EPD: Das heutige System im Überblick', section 'Gesetzlich verpflichtet versus freiwillig'
research.notes: Translation: 'For all other health professionals working in the outpatient sector, and for patients, opening an EPD is voluntary.' The two sentences before it on the page: 'Gesetzlich dazu verpflichtet sind derzeit stationäre Gesundheitseinrichtungen, die zulasten der obligatorischen Krankenpflegeversicherung (OKP) abrechnen – also Spitäler, Rehabilitationskliniken, psychiatrische Kliniken, Pflegeheime und Geburtshäuser. Seit dem 1. Januar 2022 gilt diese Regelung auch für neu zugelassene Ärztinnen und Ärzte.' ('Legally obliged at present are inpatient institutions that bill the compulsory health insurance (OKP): hospitals, rehabilitation clinics, psychiatric clinics, nursing homes and birth centres. Since 1 January 2022 this rule also applies to newly licensed doctors.') Definition: Swiss OKP is compulsory insurance run by private insurers but is the public scheme here; so OKP-billing hospitals and the self-employed ambulatory doctors who bill OKP are the brief's grey zone, not 'private'. The brief's 'private' sector is care outside OKP (private clinics not on a cantonal hospital list, self-pay or supplementary-insurance-only care, doctors without OKP admission). The BAG page ties the duty to connect to OKP billing by inpatient institutions, so providers outside OKP carry no duty, and connection for every other ambulatory provider is voluntary: a named gap, hence partial; whether any non-OKP private clinic has in fact joined an EPD community is not stated anywhere found. The operator's factsheet makes the OKP tie explicit: eHealth Suisse, 'Factsheet Wer muss ein EPD anbieten?', https://www.e-health-suisse.ch/payload/api/documents/file/Factsheet_Wer_muss_ein_EPD_anbieten.pdf (undated PDF): 'Für jede Einrichtung ist einzelfallweise zu prüfen, ob sie als Spital oder Pflegeheim nach KVG zugelassen und damit verpflichtet ist, ein EPD anzubieten.' ('For each institution it must be checked case by case whether it is admitted as a hospital or nursing home under the KVG and therefore obliged to offer an EPD'); 'Weil das Wohnheim nicht über die Krankenkasse abrechnet, ist es nicht verpflichtet, ein EPD anzubieten.' ('Because the residential home does not bill the health insurer, it is not obliged to offer an EPD'); 'Ambulant tätige Leistungserbringer, die nicht von der Revision des KVG betroffen sind, sind nicht verpflichtet, ein EPD anzubieten.' ('Outpatient providers not covered by the KVG revision are not obliged to offer an EPD'). Write vs read: the EPDG (in force since 2017, obligation for hospitals from April 2020, nursing homes and birth centres from 2022) obliges connected institutions to open and feed the EPD (the BAG page: 'Gesundheitsfachpersonen sind verpflichtet, relevante Gesundheitsinformationen im EPD zu erfassen'); the gap is on who must connect, not on write rights. Second source: eHealth Suisse, 'Aktueller Stand des EPD in der Schweiz', https://www.e-health-suisse.ch/koordination/elektronisches-patientendossier/aktueller-stand (undated, figures to end of April 2026): 'Seit 2022 sind auch neu zugelassene Arztpraxen verpflichtet, das EPD anzubieten. Die Teilnahme am EPD ist freiwillig für alle anderen Gesundheitsfachpersonen, wie vor 2022 niedergelassene Ärztinnen und Ärzte, Apothekerinnen und Apotheker, Spitex-Dienstleistende oder Physiotherapeutinnen und Physiotherapeuten.' Revision: the total revision (new Bundesgesetz über das elektronische Gesundheitsdossier, EGDG) is a bill, not law. BAG, https://www.bag.admin.ch/de/egdg : 'Da das neue Gesetz noch nicht in Kraft ist, gelten die neuen Bestimmungen derzeit noch nicht.' and 'Mit dem neuen Gesetz werden nun alle Gesundheitsfachpersonen und Gesundheitseinrichtungen, die über die obligatorische Krankenpflegeversicherung sowie die Unfall-, Invaliden- oder Militärversicherung abrechnen, verpflichtet, sich dem Informationssystem E-GD anzuschliessen und darin alle behandlungsrelevanten Daten zu erfassen'. Even that future duty is tied to OKP/UV/IV/MV billing, so purely private providers would stay outside it. The BAG page links a Federal Council release of 2025-11-05, 'Bundesrat beschliesst Neuausrichtung: E-GD löst EPD ab' (not opened: JS-only page). Date: both pages carry no publication date; the BAG page's latest dated items are factsheets 'Stand Oktober 2025' and the 2025-11-05 release. Existing country-file class was unknown (silent); this fresh evidence moves it to partial.

recordSplit.quote: The Clinic reported that public and private systems remain far from interoperable.

research.quote: La normativa afirma que el Ministerio de Salud deberá actualizar el reglamento relacionado con la ficha clínica en un plazo de dieciocho meses desde la entrada en vigencia de esta modificación, con el fin de establecer el deber de adoptar medidas que permitan que las fichas clínicas interoperen.
research.source: Ministerio de Salud de Chile (Departamento de Comunicaciones), 'Ley de interoperabilidad de fichas clínicas fue publicada en el Diario Oficial'
research.notes: Translation: 'The law states that the Ministry of Health must update the regulation on the clinical record within eighteen months of this amendment entering into force, in order to establish the duty to adopt measures that allow clinical records to interoperate.' Law in force with a future deadline = partial. Scope sentence on the same ministry page: 'La nueva ley tiene como objetivo garantizar la continuidad del cuidado del paciente con independencia de quien sea el prestador, estableciendo la interoperabilidad de la ficha clínica, tanto de prestadores públicos como privados, y fijando ciertos estándares para que esto sea posible.' ('...establishing interoperability of the clinical record for both public and private providers...'). Primary law text, Ley 21.668, Diario Oficial 28 May 2024 (CVE 2498407), https://www.diariooficial.interior.gob.cl/publicaciones/2024/05/28/43861/01/2498407.pdf : new Art. 13 of Ley 20.584 makes 'los prestadores' responsible 'de adoptar las medidas que permitan su interoperabilidad con otros prestadores de salud', and the new artículo tercero transitorio: 'El Ministerio de Salud deberá actualizar el reglamento contemplado en el artículo 13, en el plazo de dieciocho meses contado desde la entrada en vigencia de la modificación a dicho artículo, la que establece el deber de adoptar medidas tendientes a la interoperabilidad de las fichas clínicas.' Ley 20.584 applies to all prestadores, public and private, including clínicas privadas paid by Isapres or out of pocket (the 'private' of this layer). Gap as of 2026 (industry news, GesNova Salud, 11 Aug 2026, https://gesnovasalud.com/interoperabilidad-en-salud-la-ley-ya-esta-vigente-la-urgencia-ahora-es-implementarla/ ): 'Ese plazo venció en noviembre de 2025 y, a julio de 2026, el reglamento aún no ha sido publicado.' ('That deadline expired in November 2025 and, as of July 2026, the regulation has still not been published.') Vendor blogs (Surtika 4 Apr 2026, Nuvamed 23 Jun 2026) say the same. WRITE vs READ: the law imposes provider-to-provider interoperability and timely access on request; Chile has no single national record that private providers feed, so even when the reglamento lands this is a peer exchange duty, not a feed to a public record. Isapre/Fonasa links are claims links and are excluded. Against the country file: AGREES (partial, 'Public network tools exist; private links are uneven').

research.quote: 下一步，我们将按照“应接尽接”原则，重点攻坚民营医院和诊所数据接入，确保2026年底前完成全域数据汇聚。
research.source: 武汉市卫生健康委员会 (Wuhan Municipal Health Commission): 对市十五届人大六次会议第JY20260227号建议的答复 (reply to a municipal People's Congress suggestion)
research.notes: Translation: 'Next, following the principle of connecting every institution that should be connected, we will focus on tackling data connection of private hospitals and clinics, to ensure city-wide data aggregation is completed before the end of 2026.' Same reply: '完成全市民营医院、诊所标准化数据接入，补齐基层、民营机构数据短板' (complete standardised data connection of all private hospitals and clinics in the city, to fill the data shortfall of grassroots and private institutions). Kind of private: 民营医院/社会办医疗机构 (privately owned hospitals and clinics), which in China serve both basic medical insurance patients and self-pay patients; the sources speak of the institutions, not the payer. Write vs read: the platforms concerned (市级全民健康信息平台, 省卫生健康云影像/检验平台) are fed by hospital uploads; the gap named is that private hospitals and clinics do not yet upload. Second sub-national source, Suzhou Municipal Health Commission reply 苏州卫健办复〔2026〕170号, dated 2026-05-29, published 2026-06-08, http://www.suzhou.gov.cn/szsrmzf/bmwj/202606/95b1a72c8cf24b929f8a9d8fa0bc457d.shtml : '针对民营医院（社会办医疗机构），按照省卫健委“愿接尽接”的原则，有接入意愿的社会办医院可向省卫生健康信息中心申请对接' (for private hospitals, under the provincial health commission's principle of connecting those willing, private hospitals that wish to connect may apply to the provincial health information centre), against '2023年7月实现全市200余家公立医疗机构的全覆盖接入' (full coverage of 200-plus public institutions by July 2023) and '26家社会办医院已完成省影像平台对接' (26 private hospitals connected to the provincial imaging platform). National level: the NHC's September 2026 reply to NPC suggestion 0805 (https://www.nhc.gov.cn/wjw/jiany/202609/053b215bb0cd418ebb4ecfea6da5a449.shtml, page blocked to automated fetch, search snippet only) speaks of all secondary-and-above public hospitals being connected to regional platforms and is silent on private hospitals; silence is not evidence either way. China has no single national patient record (existing country file); connection is to provincial and municipal platforms, so the class rests on sub-national rules. Two municipal regulators name private hospitals and clinics as the unconnected remainder, one with a voluntary 'connect if willing' rule and one with an end-2026 deadline, so partial. Existing country file class: unknown; this research gives partial.

research.quote: Más de 1.400 prestadores de salud públicos y privados en más de 4.491 sedes interoperando, y más de 390 municipios conectados.
research.source: Ministerio de Salud y Protección Social de Colombia, 'Informe especial: Interoperabilidad de la Historia Clínica Electrónica (IHCE)', Bogotá, agosto 2026
research.notes: Translation: 'More than 1,400 public and private health providers at more than 4,491 sites interoperating, and more than 390 municipalities connected.' The sentence is hyphenated across a column break in the PDF ('prestado- res'); quoted here reconstructed. Clean cross-check in the report's footnote 17: 'Datos de agosto 4 de 2026: 21.487.483 Historias Clínicas Interoperables en formato de RDA. 6.936.927 de Historias Clínicas de pacientes.1.430 prestadores operando en 4.491 sedes de 393 municipios. En pruebas técnicas y de validación: 4.762 sedes de 1.532 prestadores en 363 municipios.' Universe from the same report: 'cerca de diez mil instituciones prestadoras de salud entre públicas y privadas, más de 19 mil sedes de atención a nivel nacional y cerca de 50.000 profesionales independientes' ('about ten thousand public and private provider institutions, more than 19 thousand care sites and about 50,000 independent professionals'). So roughly 1 in 7 providers and 1 in 4 sites are live, with a similar number in testing: only some connect = partial. WRITE: providers generate and send a Resumen Digital de Atención (RDA) to the ministry's central IHCE platform after each encounter; other authorised clinicians then query it. Rule in force covering private providers: Resolución 866 de 2021, Art. 2 (ámbito de aplicación), https://www.alcaldiabogota.gov.co/sisjur/normas/Norma1.jsp?i=114503 : '2.2 Los prestadores de servicios de salud públicos y privados.' Resolución 1888 de 2025 (15 Sep 2025), https://www.minsalud.gov.co/Normatividad_Nuevo/Resolucion%20No%201888%20de%202025.pdf , Art. 6: 'Para tal efecto, contarán con un plazo máximo de seis (6) meses, contados a partir del 15 de octubre de 2025, para integrar e interoperar sus sistemas con el modelo definido en el marco de la Interoperabilidad de la Historia Clínica Electrónica - IHCE' (deadline 15 Apr 2026, now passed, rollout progressive by territory). Resolución 1799 de 2026 (5 Aug 2026), https://www.minsalud.gov.co/sites/rid/Lists/BibliotecaDigital/RIDE/DE/DIJ/resolucion-1799-de-2026.pdf , extends scope to gestores farmacéuticos with a new deadline of six months from 1 Sep 2026. Which kind of private: most private IPS in Colombia deliver EPS-contracted, publicly financed care (contracted grey zone); the rule applies to all IPS regardless of payer, including planes voluntarios and out-of-pocket care, and the ministry count does not split by payer. Against the country file: CHANGED. File was unknown (silent); fresh primary evidence supports partial.

research.quote: Pro praxi je od 1. 1. 2026 je jedinou plošnou povinností ePoukaz. Ostatní nástroje nabíhají postupně.
research.source: Česká lékařská komora, Okresní sdružení Karlovy Vary: Elektronizace zdravotnictví od 1. 1. 2026 – přehled změn pro lékaře
research.notes: Translation: 'For practice, from 1 Jan 2026 the only universal duty is the ePoukaz [e-voucher for medical devices]. The other tools phase in gradually.' (sic: the page reads 'je od 1. 1. 2026 je'.) Same page on the shared record: 'V roce 2026 začíná postupný rozvoj sdíleného zdravotního záznamu: pouze ve vybraném, strukturovaném rozsahu, nikoli jako kompletní sdílení celé zdravotnické dokumentace.' and 'Nejde o okamžitou povinnost pro všechny lékaře'. The underlying rule is licence-based and so covers private, non-contracted providers: zákon č. 325/2021 Sb. § 34a (inserted by zákon č. 236/2025 Sb., účinnost 1. 1. 2026, https://www.zakonyprolidi.cz/cs/2021-325): '(3) Zapisující osobou údajů ... b) podle odstavce 2 písm. a) až f) je každý poskytovatel zdravotních služeb, který zjistí údaj povinně uváděný v emergentním zdravotním záznamu', with offences in § 40 for not writing; and zákon č. 372/2011 Sb. § 2 (1): 'Poskytovatelem zdravotních služeb se rozumí fyzická nebo právnická osoba, která má oprávnění k poskytování zdravotních služeb podle tohoto zákona' (no insurer-contract condition). So private providers are bound exactly like public ones, but the shared record (sdílený zdravotní záznam) is only the emergency record plus preventive/screening results, is phasing in during 2026, and full document sharing remains voluntary (30-odd hospitals per the country file). No source found that singles out private or non-contracted providers; the class rests on the licence-based definition plus the phased rollout, hence partial rather than connected. eRecept binds all prescribers but is medication only. Write, not read. Country file class was unknown; moves to partial.

research.quote: Für Vertragspraxen ist eine Institutionskarte für den Zugang zur Telematikinfrastruktur (TI) verpflichtend. Aber auch Praxen von Privatmedizinerinnen und Privatmedizinern - wie Privat(zahn)ärztinnen und Privat(zahn)ärzten oder Privatpsychotherapeutinnen und Privatpsychotherapeuten - können einen TI-Zugang erhalten.
research.source: gematik (national digital health agency, operator of the Telematikinfrastruktur and the ePA), 'Privatpraxen: Digitale Lösungen für Patienten und Praxen'
research.notes: Translation: 'For contracted (statutory-insurance) practices an institution card for access to the Telematikinfrastruktur (TI) is mandatory. But practices of private-medicine practitioners, such as private (dental) doctors or private psychotherapists, can also obtain TI access.' Kind of private: Privatärzte, i.e. doctors not admitted to vertragsärztliche Versorgung who bill patients directly (out of pocket or PKV); for them TI connection, and so the ability to write to the ePA, is optional (können), whereas for contracted practices it is mandatory. The same page: 'Privatmedizinerinnen und Privatmediziner benötigen einen Zugang zur TI unter anderem ... zum Befüllen der elektronischen Patientenakte (ePA).' Write, not read: the national ePA write duty is a statute whose scope excludes them. § 347 Abs. 1 Satz 1 SGB V (gesetze-im-internet, Stand: zuletzt geändert durch Art. 1 G v. 26.6.2026, https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/sgb_5/__347.html): 'Die an der vertragsärztlichen Versorgung teilnehmenden Leistungserbringer haben nach Maßgabe der §§ 346 und 339 Absatz 1 Daten des Versicherten ... in die elektronische Patientenakte zu übermitteln und dort zu speichern.' ('Providers participating in contracted care must transmit the insured person's data to the electronic patient record and store it there'); Abs. 2 repeats the same scope for lab results, imaging reports, procedure reports and discharge letters. Privately owned Vertragsarzt practices and plan hospitals treating GKV patients are therefore under the duty but are not 'private' under the brief; private hospitals in the Krankenhausplan are the grey zone (contracted, so in scope). Second supporting source on how far private practices actually connect: PKV-Serviceportal privat-patienten.de (run by the Verband der Privaten Krankenversicherung; page dated Dezember 2024, https://www.privat-patienten.de/digitale-services/elektronische-patientenakte-fuer-privatversicherte/): 'Vertragsarztpraxen und viele Krankenhäuser sind technisch bereits in der Lage, auf ePAs zuzugreifen und diese zu befüllen. Viele Privatpraxen und weitere medizinische Einrichtungen schaffen derzeit die Voraussetzungen dafür.' ('Contracted practices and many hospitals are already technically able to access and fill ePAs. Many private practices and other medical facilities are currently putting the prerequisites in place.'); same page: 'Erhalten alle Privatversicherten eine ePA? Nein. Die Versicherungsunternehmen entscheiden weiterhin selbst, ob sie ihren Versicherten eine ePA anbieten.' PKV-Verband provider page (https://www.pkv.de/wissen/versorgung/digitale-medizin/informationen-fuer-aerzte/was-leistunsgerbringer-zur-elektronischen-patientenakte-epa-wissen-muessen/): 'Ja, auch privatärztliche Praxen ohne Kassenzulassung können mit elektronischen Patientenakten arbeiten. Dazu müssen sie an die TI angeschlossen sein.' and 'Während gesetzliche Krankenkassen zum Angebot einer ePA verpflichtet sind, bieten private Krankenversicherungen diese auf freiwilliger Basis an.' Second kind of private, the PKV-insured patient: an ePA exists only if the insurer chooses to offer one (BMG FAQ: 'Die privaten Krankenversicherungen können ihren Versicherten ebenfalls eine ePA anbieten. Viele Anbieter bereiten dies gerade vor.', https://www.bundesgesundheitsministerium.de/themen/digitalisierung/elektronische-patientenakte/epa-fuer-alle); that insurer link is not itself a provider link. By statute the write duty also does not extend to PKV-insured records even for contracted doctors: § 362 Abs. 1 SGB V (https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/sgb_5/__362.html) lists the provisions applied 'entsprechend' to PKV ePAs ('die §§ 334 bis 337, 339, 341 Absatz 1 bis 4, § 342 Absatz 2 Nummer 1, 3 und 4 und Absatz 3, § 343 Absatz 1 und 1a, die §§ 344, 345, 352, 353, 356 bis 359a und 361') and § 347 is not among them. Tension to flag: the BMG page says 'Seit dem 1. Oktober 2025 sind alle Leistungserbringer verpflichtet, die ePA zu nutzen', but the statutory duty in § 347 is limited to providers in vertragsärztliche Versorgung; the Landesärztekammer Baden-Württemberg (24 June 2024, https://www.aerztekammer-bw.de/privataerzte-anbindung-an-die-telematikinfrastruktur-9b068ca549156fa0) likewise frames TI connection for Privatärzte as a possibility ('haben ab diesem Jahr die Möglichkeit, sich an die Telematikinfrastruktur (TI) anzuschließen'), mandatory only for implant-registry reporting. Classed partial: a rule in force covers contracted providers only; private-only practices connect voluntarily and the PKV portal says many are still building the capability; no source found saying almost none connect, so not split. The existing country file is silent (unknown); this is new evidence, so it does not agree or disagree with a prior class.

research.quote: Du kan se notater og epikriser fra alle offentlige hospitaler samt en stadig stigende andel af privathospitaler.
research.source: sundhed.dk (the Danish national health portal, owned by the regions, state and municipalities), FAQ for health professionals: Fejl eller manglende data i Sundhedsjournalen, item 'Der mangler Journalnotater/epikriser i Sundhedsjournalen'
research.notes: Translation: 'You can see notes and discharge summaries from all public hospitals and from a steadily growing share of private hospitals.' Same item continues: 'Du kan endnu ikke se: notater fra praktiserende læger, praktiserende speciallæger og kommuner.' and the Aftaler item says 'Du kan ikke se aftaler fra privathospitaler og privatklinikker.' Page shows 'Opdateret 16.12.2025'. Second source, the citizen FAQ 'Spørgsmål om Journaler' (https://www.sundhed.dk/borger/service/kontakt/hjaelp-borger/dine-sundhedsdata/sporgsmaal-om-journal-fra-sygehus/, 'Fagligt opdateret 10.12.2024'): 'de fleste privathospitaler: Fra april 2020 er privathospitaler begyndt at levere journaldata. Det er dog ikke alle privathospitaler, der leverer data, og det er derfor ikke sikkert, du kan se oplysninger fra din behandling.' (most private hospitals: from April 2020 private hospitals began delivering journal data. Not all private hospitals deliver data, however, so it is not certain you can see information from your treatment), and under 'Hvor kan jeg ikke se journaler fra' it lists 'nogle privathospitaler'. Kind of private: privathospitaler and privatklinikker, i.e. the private hospital sector that treats both self-pay/privately insured patients and publicly referred patients; the data feed is per hospital, not per payer, so self-pay care at a connected private hospital is written and care at a non-connected one is not. Separate register duty in force: Bekendtgørelse nr. 1496 af 1. december 2016 § 1 'Oplysninger om lægelig behandling af patienter på private sygehuse eller klinikker skal anmeldes til Landspatientregisteret efter reglerne i denne bekendtgørelse.' with § 3 defining private as 'alle behandlingssteder, hvor der foregår lægelig behandling, og som ikke fuldt ud ejes eller drives af offentlige myndigheder' (https://www.retsinformation.dk/eli/lta/2016/1496/pdf, in force 1 January 2017); that is reporting to the national patient register, not a clinical note feed, and is noted here but is not the basis of the class. Note: sundhed.dk pages are JavaScript-only for ordinary clients; the text above was read from the server-rendered version the site serves to search-engine crawlers. Write (delivering journal data) with read effects; the class rests on the write gap. Country file class was unknown; moves to partial. [Parent re-check 2026-10-01: sundhed.dk renders by script and returned no text to curl or WebFetch; quote rests on the research agent's rendered read.]

research.quote: He also confirmed that eHealth is preparing to launch standardized digital solutions in the near future to integrate private-sector actors—such as primary and specialty clinics, pharmacies, and hospitals—into the national digital health ecosystem.
research.source: eHealth (state-affiliated company set up by Prime Ministerial Decree No. 2118 of 2021 to operate the Universal Health Insurance System's technology services; eFinance Group), press release 'Ministry of Health and "eHealth" Collaborate to Operate the National Digital Health System'
research.notes: English source (operator page). Class unknown: the sentence names private clinics, pharmacies and hospitals but speaks of future 'ecosystem' integration with no deadline, and does not say whether private providers write to the Egypt Healthcare Authority / Universal Health Insurance electronic record; it is the IT operator's forward statement about its own products. Alternative reading: a reader applying the brief's 'names a gap' clause could class this partial, since the sentence implies private clinics, pharmacies and hospitals are not yet integrated; unknown was chosen because the statement is the operator's product roadmap, speaks to ecosystem integration rather than writing to the EHA/UHI record, and gives no deadline. The Arabic coverage of the same 3 June 2025 agreement (Al-Shorouk, https://www.shorouknews.com/mobile/news/view.aspx?cdate=03062025&id=5f2b4b8e-2612-4893-8bc3-7a2a2184bfac) does not carry a private-sector integration sentence. Other sources opened: UHIA contracting conditions, https://uhia.gov.eg/إجراءات-التعاقد/ : 'ضرورة أن يمتلك مقدم الخدمة الطبية التجهيزات الإلكترونية اللازمة للتعامل مع البطاقات والمستندات لإتمام عملية تقديم الخدمة الطبية' (the provider must have the electronic equipment needed to handle cards and documents to complete service delivery), an insurer/claims link, excluded by the brief. UHIA FAQ says the family medical file is opened at the primary care unit. Youm7, 2026-09-30, https://www.youm7.com/story/2026/9/30/%D9%86%D8%A7%D8%A6%D8%A8-%D9%88%D8%B2%D9%8A%D8%B1-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B5%D8%AD%D8%A9-%D9%8A%D8%A8%D8%AD%D8%AB-%D8%AA%D8%B7%D8%A8%D9%8A%D9%82-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%B3%D8%AA%D8%B1%D8%A7%D8%AA%D9%8A%D8%AC%D9%8A%D8%A9-%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%88%D8%B7%D9%86%D9%8A%D8%A9-%D9%84%D9%84%D8%B5%D8%AD%D8%A9-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B1%D9%82%D9%85%D9%8A%D8%A9/7563209 : the Deputy Minister's meeting 'أكد على أهمية تفعيل منظومة تبادل المعلومات الصحية HIE بصورة آمنة وفعالة' (stressed the importance of activating the health information exchange, HIE, securely and effectively), which shows the national exchange is still being set up; it does not mention private providers. Kind of private: contracted private providers under UHI (grey zone) and fully private providers outside UHI are both unaddressed by any opened primary. Agrees with the existing class in the country file (unknown).

research.quote: La Comunidad de Madrid y Galicia son las únicas regiones que comparten datos entre las dos redes sanitarias
research.source: Redacción Médica, "Paso a la historia abierta: un 23% de médicos ya ve la del SNS y la privada" (page title: ¿Qué CCAA integran la historia clínica en pública y privada?)
research.notes: (The sentence is the article's subheading and carries no closing full stop.) Translation: "The Comunidad de Madrid and Galicia are the only regions that share data between the two healthcare networks." Class is partial because only some private providers connect, and only in some regions; the same page states the national picture: "La mayoría de comunidades autónomas no tienen implantada la historia clínica digital interoperable entre la sanidad pública y la sanidad privada." (Most autonomous communities have not implemented a digital clinical record interoperable between public and private healthcare.) only the Comunidad de Madrid and Galicia share records between the two networks; Navarra, Aragón, Extremadura, Murcia and Andalucía share only with contracted (concertado) centres; ten regions including Cataluña keep the record exclusively in the public network. Galicia's IANUS has included private/contracted hospitals since 2009 (write). NATIONAL RECORD: the HCDSNS is built only from the regional SNS services; Ministry of Health page (undated): "Es un sistema que permite a las Comunidades Autónomas compartir información clínica relevante para que esté disponible en soporte electrónico, en cualquier servicio autonómico del SNS, a petición de los ciudadanos." (https://www.sanidad.gob.es/areas/saludDigital/historiaClinicaSNS/home.htm). It is silent on private care; silence is not used for the class. The private sector runs its own separate interoperability platform (Fundación IDIS miHC: 16 insurer and hospital groups, 400,000 users, 1 million accesses, 12 Mar 2025, https://innovaidis.com/publicaciones/espacio-de-datos-de-la-sanidad-privada/la-fundacion-idis-presenta-su-proyecto-de-espacio-de-datos-de-la-sanidad-privada-edsp/); the Madrid private hospitals association ACHPM (4 Jul 2022) said the reform of RD 1093/2010 "no contempla la sanidad privada" (https://achpm.es/achpm-denuncia-exclusion/). SUB-NATIONAL PRIMARY SOURCES: Madrid, Ley 11/2022 de 21 de diciembre (BOE-A-2023-7343, https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2023-7343): amends arts. 22 and 25 of Ley 12/2001 "con el fin de que se pueda compartir la historia clínica entre entidades públicas y privadas promoviendo la colaboración entre las mismas" (mainly consent-based read access for private doctors, 'y viceversa'). Catalonia, CatSalut Instrucció 19.11.2018 "Documentació clínica aportada pels ciutadans emesa per professionals sanitaris i centres sanitaris no pertanyents al SISCAT per a la inclusió a la història clínica compartida de Catalunya (HC3)" (https://www.uch.cat/documents/documentaci-clnica.pdf): documents from non-SISCAT (private) providers enter HC3 only when the citizen brings them and a SISCAT professional publishes them, i.e. patient-mediated, not a provider feed; HC3 publishing web services are for SISCAT providers (https://web.gencat.cat/ca/generalitat/com-ens-organitzem/departaments/salut/ambits/tic/solucions-siscat/cataleg/historia-clinica-compartida-catalunya-hc3). Redacción Médica 26 Sep 2025: the Departament de Salut contracted a platform so imaging from private centres can be uploaded to HC3/La Meva Salut with patient consent (not yet live). WRITE vs READ: the 2022 survey mostly measures doctors' ability to view both records; writing by fully private (non-contracted) providers into a public record is documented only for Galicia; elsewhere it is contracted providers (grey zone) or patient uploads. KIND OF PRIVATE: both insurer-paid/out-of-pocket private centres (excluded nationally) and concertados (connected in some regions). AGREEMENT WITH FILE: file class was unknown (silent); this evidence moves Spain to partial. The most explicit national statement is from Dec 2022; no newer national source found that contradicts it, and the 2025 Catalonia contract points the same way.

research.quote: Levinud on arusaam, et tasuliste teenuste andmeid ei pea tervise infosüsteemi esitama, mis tekitab andmelünki.
research.source: Riigikontroll (National Audit Office of Estonia), news release: Sotsiaalministeeriumil tuleks jõulisemalt seista korrektsete terviseandmete talletamise eest
research.notes: Translation: 'A widespread understanding is that data on paid services need not be submitted to the health information system, which creates data gaps.' Next sentence on the page: 'Näiteks leidub hambaraviasutusi, mis on info ravi kohta sisestanud suure viivitusega või ei ole oma patsientide kohta infosüsteemi ühtki dokumenti esitanud.' (For example there are dental care institutions that entered treatment information with great delay or have not submitted a single document about their patients.) Kind of private: self-pay services (tasulised teenused), incl. private dental clinics, i.e. care paid outside Tervisekassa. The write duty itself is licence-based, not contract-based: Tervishoiuteenuste korraldamise seadus § 59² (1) 'Tervishoiuteenuse osutaja on kohustatud edastama tervise infosüsteemi andmed' and § 4 (1) 'Tervishoiuteenuse osutaja on tervishoiutöötaja või tervishoiuteenuseid osutav juriidiline isik' (consolidated text with amendments to RT I, 28.04.2026, read at https://estlex.ee/oigusakt/tervishoiuteenuste-korraldamise-seadus). So every licensed provider, public or private, must write to TIS, but the state auditor says paid-service data are in practice often not submitted: a gap named by an audit body, hence partial rather than connected. Write, not read. Country file class was unknown (silent on private providers); moves to partial.

recordSplit.quote: In Nouvelle-Aquitaine 90% of health establishments and 68.5% of private professionals feed it

research.quote: Dans le respect des règles déontologiques qui lui sont applicables ainsi que des articles L. 1110-4, L. 1470-5 et L. 1111-2, chaque professionnel de santé, quels que soient son mode et son lieu d'exercice, doit reporter dans le dossier médical partagé, à l'occasion de chaque acte ou consultation, les éléments diagnostiques et thérapeutiques nécessaires à la coordination des soins de la personne prise en charge, dont la liste est fixée par arrêté du ministre chargé de la santé.
research.source: Légifrance, Code de la santé publique, article L1111-15 (version en vigueur depuis le 01/01/2024, modifié par LOI n°2021-1018 du 2 août 2021 art. 16)
research.notes: Translation: 'In compliance with the ethical rules applicable to them and with articles L. 1110-4, L. 1470-5 and L. 1111-2, every health professional, whatever their mode and place of practice, must record in the shared medical record (DMP), on the occasion of each act or consultation, the diagnostic and therapeutic elements needed to coordinate the care of the person treated, the list of which is set by order of the minister for health.' Kind of private: 'quels que soient son mode et son lieu d'exercice' reaches practitioners outside the Assurance Maladie conventions (secteur 3 / non conventionnés) and those working in cliniques privées, not only libéraux who bill the public scheme. The same article covers establishments without distinguishing ownership: 'A l'occasion du séjour d'une personne prise en charge, les professionnels de santé habilités des établissements de santé doivent reporter dans le dossier médical partagé, dans le respect des obligations définies par la Haute Autorité de santé, un résumé des principaux éléments relatifs à ce séjour.' Write, not read: 'reporter dans le dossier médical partagé' is a write obligation; the DMP is the medical-record component of Mon espace santé. Second supporting source: Arrêté du 26 avril 2022 fixant la liste des documents soumis à l'obligation prévue à l'article L. 1111-15, art. 2 (text reproduced at https://www.departement-information-medicale.com/pieces-a-verser-au-dmp/): 'Les médecins et les biologistes concernés, quels que soient leur mode et leur lieu d'exercice, sont tenus de respecter l'obligation prévue à l'article 1er' ('the doctors and biologists concerned, whatever their mode and place of practice, are bound by the obligation in article 1'); amended by arrêté du 23 mai 2024. Legifrance blocks non-browser fetches; the quote was read through a fetch of the Legifrance page and checked word for word against the mirror at https://www.hopitalex.com/donnees-juridiques?action=affichedoc&doc=12924 (May 2024). Gap check: no source found that names a private-specific gap. Official usage figures are not split by ownership: REPSS Maladie indicator 2.9.4 (evaluation.securite-sociale.fr, data to 31/12/2025, https://evaluation.securite-sociale.fr/home/maladie/284-personnes-disposant-dun-doss.html): '2 médecins de ville sur 3 versent des documents' and '90% des établissements de santé y transmettent des documents, avec notamment 2 lettres de liaison sur 3 qui sont ainsi envoyées systématiquement'. Cnam deputy director Marguerite Cazeneuve to the Senate social affairs committee, week of 17 February 2025 (https://www.senat.fr/compte-rendu-commissions/20250217/soci.html): 'Deux tiers des établissements de santé, tant publics que privés, ont fait appel au programme national de mise à jour des logiciels' (two thirds of health establishments, public and private alike, used the national software-upgrade programme), so cliniques privées are inside the Ségur feeding programme. Enforcement: I found no penalty attached to L1111-15 itself; the only lever in the code is L1111-14, which conditions adherence to the national conventions on consulting or updating the DMP, and that lever by construction does not reach non-conventionné practitioners. The Cour des comptes RALFSS 2024 chapter on Mon espace santé (ccomptes.fr) could not be fetched from this environment (connection refused), so it is not relied on. Agrees with the existing country-file class (connected), but on a better-fitting sentence: the file's '150,000 private practitioners and 3,800 institutions' (an Assurance Maladie figure) counts libéraux who bill the public scheme, whereas L1111-15 binds every professional regardless of mode of practice. [Parent re-check 2026-10-01: Legifrance blocks curl; WebFetch read confirmed the opening clause of L1111-15, version in force 01/01/2024.]

research.quote: No independent prescribing organisations currently have ‘write access’ to patients’ NHS medical records – that is, the ability to enter information directly into a record.
research.source: Health Services Safety Investigations Body (HSSIB), Online prescribing: challenges and opportunities to improve patient safety, investigation report
research.notes: English, no translation needed. Kind of private: independent (private) prescribing organisations, i.e. online and private prescribers paid outside the NHS; the sentence is about WRITE access to the NHS record (the GP-held record and the national Summary Care Record / National Care Records Service derived from it). Same report, para 64-65: the GP is data controller of the NHS record and some GPs replied that information about a private prescription would not be filed because "it was a private prescription and therefore should not form part of the NHS record". READ access, second source (NHS England staff reply on the NHS England Developer Community forum, 2026-05-13, support only): https://developer.community.nhs.uk/t/scr-use-cases-for-private-nhs-providers/12022 : "Providers of Private Care are not currently in scope of approval for rollout of Summary Care Record viewing access:" and "Proof of concept pilots are currently in progress within non-approved care settings." Grey zone: independent-sector providers that hold an NHS contract can apply for SCR viewing (read only); IHPN's 10 Year Plan submission (Dec 2024, https://www.ihpn.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/10-year-plan-for-health-submission-December-2024.pdf ) lists "Access to patient care records not being routinely shared with independent providers" as a barrier. The Health Bill introduced in the Commons on 14 May 2026 (not in force) would let regulations require information from "NHS and private providers of health and care services" for a Single Patient Record (Explanatory Notes para 391, as quoted by Burges Salmon, 2026-05-22); a bill not in force does not move the class. Evidence is England only; Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland were not checked. Existing class in the country file: unknown. This changes it to split. [EDITOR FLAG: split rests on one private segment (independent prescribing organisations) plus a read-side scope statement from an NHS England forum reply. No source found either way on private hospitals writing to the record. England only.]
research.editorRuling: JAS-delegated 1 Oct 2026: England evidence covers independent prescribers only (no write access); nothing on private hospitals, so partial, not split.

research.quote: The challenge with this arrangement has been the difficulty in getting the Teaching Hospitals, Quasi-government facilities and some private hospitals to align to this epidemiological (person, place, and time) reporting as they do not see their facilities as being part of the district health system.
research.source: Ministry of Health, Ghana, Health Information System Strategic Plan 2022-2025 (HISSP), June 2022
research.notes: English source (PDF). The sentence concerns aggregate service reporting into DHIMS2 (district health information system), not the patient-level record in LHIMS/GHIMS, so it does not answer whether private facilities write to the shared record; class stays unknown. Same document: 'Public and private facilities use either manual or electronic means to register and document the services that they offer to clients' and strategy 4.3 'Expand the coverage of private health sector service data in the national database', again about aggregate data. Other sources opened: Graphic Online opinion, 2026-07-31, https://www.graphic.com.gh/features/opinion/ghana-news-interoperability-ghanas-national-health-information-exchange-building-a-connected-health-system.html : 'Despite these investments, health information in Ghana remains fragmented across multiple platforms, databases, and healthcare facilities that operate independently' (no mention of private facilities). Scoping review, PMC13085690 (2026): 'interoperability remains limited to partial or one-directional data exchange' (no private-facility statement). Health Informatics Journal 2026, doi 10.1177/14604582261460299, abstract via Europe PMC: four private hospitals in Suame ran their own EHRS used for 'streamlined documentation and claims processing'; the abstract does not say whether these systems connect to LHIMS or GHIMS (full text subscription-only, not opened). Agrees with the existing class in the country file (unknown: 'private facilities were not shown to be connected').

research.quote: Ως ημερομηνία έναρξης πιλοτικής εφαρμογής καταχώρησης των αποτελεσμάτων Διαγνωστικών Εργαστηριακών Εξετάσεων στο Ψηφιακό Αποθετήριο, ορίζεται η 01η/09/2026 και για διάστημα 2 μηνών, ενώ από 01/11/2026 καθίσταται υποχρεωτική η εφαρμογή του άρθρου 3 της υπ' αρ Γ.Π.οικ.974 (ΦΕΚ Β 1503/17.03.2026) ΚΥΑ ως προς τα αναφερόμενα στην αποζημίωση των διαγνωστικών εξετάσεων.
research.source: ΕΟΠΥΥ (Εθνικός Οργανισμός Παροχής Υπηρεσιών Υγείας), notice ΔΒ2Β/509/οικ.20022 "Έναρξη πιλοτικής εφαρμογής καταχώρησης των αποτελεσμάτων Διαγνωστικών Εργαστηριακών Εξετάσεων στο Ψηφιακό Αποθετήριο από 01/09/2026 και μετάθεση υποχρεωτικότητας στην αποζημίωση σε 01/11/2026" (landing page https://www.eopyy.gov.gr/el/arthra/enarksi-pilotikis-efarmogis-katahorisis-ton-apotelesmaton-diagnostikon-ergastiriakon-eksetaseon-sto-psifiako-apothetirio-apo-01092026-kai-metathesi-ypohreotikotitas-stin-apozimiosi-se-01112026/)
research.notes: CLASS REASON: partial because (a) the rule in force that makes private units write lab results to the national Repository is enforced only from 1 Nov 2026 and only for EOPYY-contracted units and EOPYY-paid tests, and (b) uploads of out-of-pocket diagnostics by private centres are described as optional. This overturns the file's 'connected', which rested on e-prescription/e-referral, a separate flow. Translation: "The start date of the pilot for recording diagnostic laboratory test results in the Digital Repository is set at 01/09/2026 for a period of 2 months, while from 01/11/2026 the application of article 3 of joint ministerial decision Γ.Π.οικ.974 (Government Gazette B 1503/17.03.2026) becomes mandatory as regards the reimbursement of diagnostic tests." RULE IN FORCE (general): Law 4600/2019 art. 84 (FEK A 43, 9 Mar 2019), para 5: "Οι ιατροί, οι οδοντίατροι και οι άλλοι επαγγελματίες υγείας, οι οποίοι είναι πιστοποιημένοι και εξουσιοδοτημένοι χρήστες του Συστήματος της Ηλεκτρονικής Συνταγογράφησης (ΣΗΣ), υποχρεούνται να καταχωρούν στον Α.Η.Φ.Υ. όλες τις πληροφορίες που προκύπτουν από εξέταση ή επίσκεψη" (https://www.e-nomothesia.gr/kat-ygeia/nomos-4600-2019-phek-43a-9-3-2019.html): every e-prescription-certified doctor, public or private, must write visit data to the personal health record. RULE IN FORCE (diagnostics): KYA Γ.Π.οικ.974, FEK B 1503/17.03.2026, new para 3 (https://www.posipy.gr/images/stories/DOCS/kataxorisi%20apotelesm1503.pdf): "Ειδικότερα, οι δημόσιες και ιδιωτικές μονάδες υγείας που είναι συμβεβλημένες με τον ΕΟΠΥΥ, δεν θα αποζημιώνονται τις διαγνωστικές εργαστηριακές εξετάσεις των οποίων το αποτέλεσμα δεν θα έχουν καταχωρήσει στο Ψηφιακό Αποθετήριο Διαγνωστικών Εργαστηριακών Αποτελεσμάτων"; enforcement reaches only EOPYY-contracted units and EOPYY-paid tests (grey-zone private), payment-linked from 1 Nov 2026 (future deadline, hence partial). NAMED GAP for private-pay care: Ygeiamou 13 May 2026, on IDIKA information (https://www.ygeiamou.gr/idisis/politiki-igias/560917/kanate-exetasis-se-nosokomio-tou-esi-dite-ta-apotelesmata-sto-myhealthapp/): "Παρότι η ενημέρωση από τα διαγνωστικά του Αποθετηρίου είναι προαιρετική, όποια εξέταση αποζημιώνεται από τον Εθνικό Οργανισμό Παροχής Υπηρεσιών Υγείας (ΕΟΠΥΥ), δηλαδή προκύπτει από παραπεμπτικό μέσω ΕΟΠΥΥ, φορτώνεται στον ΕΗΦΥ." (uploads by private diagnostic centres are optional; only EOPYY-reimbursed tests reach the national record). Ethnos 26 May 2025: the record "δεν αναμένεται να περιλαμβάνει τα ιατρικά αρχεία των ασθενών από τα νοσοκομεία" yet; same article: EIFY in full operation "για όλο το ιατρικό προσωπικό της χώρας, τόσο του ιδιωτικού όσο και του δημόσιου τομέα" and doctors "θα πρέπει να καταγράφουν τις επισκέψεις" (write by private doctors). OPERATOR CLAIM, IDIKA 27 May 2025 (https://www.idika.gr/enarxi-katholikis-efarmogis-tis-neas-psifiakis-platformas-tou-esy-gia-ton-ethniko-ilektroniko-fakelo-ygeias-eify/): "Πρόσβαση σε όλα τα δεδομένα των ασθενών από όλους τους παρόχους υγείας, σε όλες τις βαθμίδες του δημόσιου και ιδιωτικού τομέα." WRITE vs READ: private doctors on e-prescription have a legal write duty; private diagnostic centres write to the Repository optionally unless EOPYY-paid; for private clinics the EOPYY rule covers contracted ones and lab results only. KIND OF PRIVATE: law covers all; enforced feeding covers EOPYY-contracted (grey zone); out-of-pocket diagnostics named as optional. AGREEMENT WITH FILE: file GRC was connected on e-prescription and e-referral since 2010; this disagrees. E-prescription is a separate flow; for the health record itself, sources in force name gaps and a future deadline, so partial.
