research.quote: Berdasarkan data Satu Sehat, per 27 Oktober 2025, tercatat 34.463 fasyankes telah berhasil terintegrasi dengan Satu Sehat, namun Kemenkes mengakui masih adanya tantangan besar di daerah, seperti infrastruktur dan kesiapan sumber daya manusia.
research.source: Badan Kebijakan Pembangunan Kesehatan (BKPK), Kementerian Kesehatan RI: 'Wajib Integrasi Satu Sehat, Kemenkes Desak Percepatan RME di Fasyankes'
research.notes: Translation: 'Based on Satu Sehat data, as of 27 October 2025, 34,463 health facilities had successfully integrated with Satu Sehat, but the Ministry of Health acknowledges there are still major challenges in the regions, such as infrastructure and human-resource readiness.' Same page: 'meskipun batas akhir integrasi RME sempat ditargetkan pada 31 Desember 2023, target tersebut diundur hingga akhir 2025 karena adanya berbagai hambatan' (the RME integration deadline, originally 31 Dec 2023, was pushed to end-2025 because of obstacles) and '3.138 dari 3.239 rumah sakit (RS) yang telah menerapkan RME' (3,138 of 3,239 hospitals run an EMR). RULE IN FORCE (write obligation, all ownership types): Permenkes 24/2022 tentang Rekam Medis (enacted 31 Aug 2022; status 'Berlaku' per peraturan.bpk.go.id/Details/245544 (search result, page not opened)), https://keslan.kemkes.go.id/unduhan/fileunduhan_1662611251_882318.pdf: Pasal 3(1) 'Setiap Fasilitas Pelayanan Kesehatan wajib menyelenggarakan Rekam Medis Elektronik.' (every health facility must run an electronic medical record), Pasal 3(2) lists tempat praktik mandiri, puskesmas, klinik, rumah sakit, apotek, laboratorium, balai, with no ownership carve-out; Pasal 21 'Rekam Medis Elektronik yang disimpan oleh Fasilitas Pelayanan Kesehatan harus terhubung/terinteroperabilitas dengan platform layanan interoperabilitas dan integrasi data kesehatan yang dikelola oleh Kementerian Kesehatan.' (the EMR kept by a facility must be connected/interoperable with the ministry-run interoperability platform, i.e. SATUSEHAT); Pasal 45 deadline 31 Desember 2023 (passed). Kind of private: all privately owned facilities (private hospitals, klinik, independent practices, pharmacies), whether BPJS-contracted or self-pay; the rule does not distinguish. Write, not read: the obligation is to send EMR data to SATUSEHAT. Gap named by the ministry itself: 34,463 integrated against a universe the minister put at roughly 100,000 facilities (existing country file), deadline slipped from 2023 to end-2025, and in March 2026 the Ditjen Keslan letter YM.02.02/D/971/2026 sanctioned 1,306 hospitals (accreditation downgrades, 11 licence suspensions) for not meeting SATUSEHAT-integrated RME, per RSUD dr. M. Haulussy Maluku, https://rsudhaulussy.malukuprov.go.id/artikel/XN0MWZMxoR (2026-04-01): 'terdapat 1.306 rumah sakit yang masuk dalam kategori sanksi' (read through a summarising fetch, not copied from raw page text; supporting detail only, the class does not rest on it). Rule covers private providers and names a passed-then-extended deadline plus incomplete integration, so partial rather than connected. Existing country file class: unknown (silent on private); this research gives partial.

research.quote: Only ~26,000 facilities actively transact on the platform, predominantly government facilities (~21,000), while private-sector participation remains low (~4,000).
research.source: Health and Population: Perspectives and Issues (NIHFW journal), Shanmugam H, Rawat S, 'Challenges in Implementing the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission in India: A Perspective from a Private Personal Health Record Implementer', 2026;49(2):180-184
research.notes: English source. The sentence is printed contiguously on p. 180 of the PDF; pdftotext collapses the spaces in 'private-sector participation remains low' on that line, so a text-match check should normalise spaces. WRITE: under ABDM, a facility acting as Health Information Provider pushes the records it generates to the patient's ABHA (Ayushman Bharat Health Account) on the patient's consent; the quoted sentence counts facilities that actually transact, so it is a write measure. Why partial, not split: the paper says private participation is 'low', not absent, and the same paragraph says '~1.1 lakh facilities actively link health records to ABHA' (1 lakh = 100,000; 1 crore = 10 million). The paragraph is internally inconsistent (~26,000 'transact' vs ~1.1 lakh 'link'); do not lean on either number alone. Caveats: this is a perspective paper by authors at a private PHR platform (declared), and its figures cite the ABDM dashboard (dashboard.abdm.gov.in), which blocked our fetch, so the public/private split of the Health Facility Registry was not read from a primary page and is unknown here. Which kind of private: ABDM's private participants include both PM-JAY-empanelled hospitals (contracted, publicly funded care, grey zone) and purely out-of-pocket private hospitals, clinics and labs; no primary source found splits them. Participation is incentive-based, not mandated. Second source (primary): Rajya Sabha Unstarred Question 1885, answered 16 Dec 2025 by MoS Health Prataprao Jadhav, https://sansad.in/getFile/annex/269/AU1885_I2c3GM.pdf?source=pqars : 'The Digital Health Incentive Scheme (DHIS) was launched in January 2023 under which financial incentives are provided to both public and private healthcare facilities and healthtech companies to encourage participation in the ABDM ecosystem.' and 'As a result, adoption among private and smaller providers has grown steadily, contributing to wider coverage and interoperability under ABDM.' Third (primary, totals only, no public/private split): PIB release 2288848, 24 Jul 2026, https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2288848 : 'As of 20th July 2026, 5.36 lakh facilities are registered on the HFR.' Registration on HFR is not the same as writing records. Against the country file: DISAGREES. File class was unknown (its '450+ public and private solutions integrated' sentence is about software). Fresh evidence supports partial: private facilities do write to ABHA-linked records, but only a minority of them do.

research.quote:
It is a secure clinical system that gives authorised healthcare staff read-only access to key patient information from various sources. These include:
hospitals
primary care
community services
eventually, private healthcare providers
research.source: Health Service Executive (HSE), HSE Shared Care Record
research.notes: English, no translation needed. The four items after "These include:" are bullet-list items on the page, joined here with newlines; the clause the class rests on is the fourth bullet, "eventually, private healthcare providers". The page is marked beta and carries no date; it describes the first release in November 2025, national release in early 2026 and one further data release planned for 2026. Kind of private: private healthcare providers generally (private hospitals, private GPs, self-pay or insured). WRITE: today's sources are HSE statutory hospitals, some voluntary hospitals, GP-requested laboratory and radiology results, PCRS medications and NIO vaccinations; private providers feed it only "eventually". Clinicians have read-only access ("Users are not able to input or edit data on the SCR"). Second source, the Health Information Act 2026 (No. 10 of 2026, signed 30 April 2026), https://www.irishstatutebook.ie/eli/2026/act/10/enacted/en/print.html : "health services provider" means, among others, "a body corporate, or an unincorporated body of persons, through which or in connection with which (whether by reason of employment or otherwise) a health practitioner provides a health service", so private providers are in scope. Section 7 (duty to forward personal health data to another provider treating the patient) is "Not yet commenced"; section 19 (the HSE may request a provider to supply personal health data for the national Electronic Health Record; "A health services provider shall comply with a request under subsection (2).") commenced 17 August 2026 by the Health Information Act 2026 (Commencement) Order 2026, per https://www.irishstatutebook.ie/eli/isbc/2026_10.html . Section 19 works request by request, not as a standing feed. Existing class in the country file: unknown. This changes it to partial.

research.quote: נכון לדצמבר 2013, הגופים הבאים היו מחוברים למערכת שיתוף המידע: ארבע קופות החולים, בתי החולים של שירותי בריאות כללית, בתי החולים הממשלתיים הכלליים ובתי החולים הדסה בירושלים ולניאדו בנתניה.
research.source: המכון הלאומי לחקר שרותי הבריאות ומדיניות הבריאות (Israel National Institute for Health Policy Research): ספר כנס ים-המלח ה-16, 'נתוני בריאות: קריאה להסדרה', footnote 12 citing מרכז המחקר והמידע של הכנסת, 'רשומה רפואית לאומית', 14 May 2014, p. 8
research.notes: Translation: 'As of December 2013, the following bodies were connected to the information-sharing system: the four health funds, the hospitals of Clalit Health Services, the government general hospitals, and the Hadassah hospitals in Jerusalem and Laniado in Netanya.' This is a 2013 participant list, relayed in a 2016 conference book from a 2014 Knesset research paper; it names only HMOs and public (government, Clalit, Hadassah, Laniado) hospitals and says nothing either way about private hospitals (Assuta, Herzliya Medical Center) or private clinics, so the omission is not evidence. The Ministry of Health's current Eitan page (https://www.gov.il/he/pages/shared-medical-info) is rendered by JavaScript and returned 403 to automated fetch, so its participant list could not be read. A Knesset Science and Technology Committee transcript of 20 Dec 2010 (https://oknesset.org/meetings/4/0/402817.html) records, in a discussion of the planned national medical record, the question 'מה עם בתי חולים פרטיים?' answered 'זה כולל את כל בתי החולים' (it includes all hospitals), but that was a 2010 plan, not a statement about Eitan as built, and it was read through a summarising fetch rather than copied from the page. Kind of private that matters: private hospitals paid by supplementary HMO insurance (שב"ן), private insurers or out of pocket (Assuta is Maccabi-owned, so it is a grey zone; Herzliya Medical Center is independent), and private clinics. No ministry, operator, comptroller or peer-reviewed source opened says whether these providers write to Eitan. Searches in Hebrew and English for 'איתן' with 'בתי חולים פרטיים', 'אסותא', 'הרצליה מדיקל סנטר' returned nothing on point. Silence is unknown. Existing country file class: unknown; this research keeps unknown. research.quote: Pertanto, in assenza di specifiche disposizioni regionali che dispongano diversamente, il libero professionista medico o odontoiatra in regime privatistico puro non risulta destinatario di un obbligo diretto e automatico di alimentazione del FSE analogo a quello previsto per i soggetti del SSN, potendosi, eventualmente, se e ove previsto, configurare invece un’eventuale facoltà del professionista in tal senso.
research.source: FNOMCeO (Federazione Nazionale degli Ordini dei Medici Chirurghi e degli Odontoiatri), Comunicazione Prot. 3562/2026 del 05.03.2026 to OMCeO Sassari, reply to an ANDI query on FSE feeding and e-prescription obligations (PDF hosted by OMCeO Sassari; reproduced by OMCeO Milano 6 Mar 2026, https://omceomi.it/2026/03/06/fascicolo-sanitario-elettronico/29491/)
research.notes: Translation: "Therefore, absent specific regional provisions to the contrary, a doctor or dentist practising purely privately as a freelancer is not subject to a direct and automatic obligation to feed the FSE comparable to that laid on SSN bodies; where provided for, it may instead be an option for the professional." (The PDF has a stray space before the final full stop; otherwise verbatim.) RULE IN FORCE: art. 12 c.1 DL 179/2012 as amended (DL 34/2020 art. 11 and later), normattiva consolidated text: "Ai fini del presente comma, ogni prestazione sanitaria erogata da operatori pubblici, privati accreditati e privati autorizzati è inserita, entro cinque giorni dalla prestazione medesima, nel FSE in conformità alle disposizioni del presente articolo." (https://www.normattiva.it/uri-res/N2Ls?urn:nir:stato:decreto.legge:2012-10-18;179~art12) and c.3: feeding by professionals who treat the patient "sia nell'ambito del Servizio sanitario nazionale ... sia al di fuori degli stessi". Ministry FSE portal (https://www.fascicolosanitario.gov.it/): "I dati e i documenti sono riferiti a prestazioni erogate dal Servizio Sanitario Nazionale (SSN) e, a partire dal 19 maggio 2020, anche da strutture sanitarie private." So accredited (grey zone) and merely authorised private structures, including those working only in regime di solvenza (out of pocket), must write. NAMED GAPS: FNOMCeO above (pure libero-professionisti, i.e. private practices not organised as an authorised struttura, have no feeding duty and no sanction); DM 11 novembre 2025 (GU n.286, 10 Dec 2025, text via https://farmaciavirtuale.it/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/5906-Estratto-Gazzetta-Ufficiale-Serie-generale-n.-286-del-10-dicembre-2025.pdf) kept FSE 2.0 "III fase - entro e non oltre il 31 marzo 2026", the phase in which regions enable feeding by non-accredited private structures (deadline now passed); Agenda Digitale 20 Jul 2026 (https://www.agendadigitale.eu/sanita/fse-2-0-privacy-e-nuovi-obblighi-per-le-strutture-private/): until then feeding "è rimasta un adempimento sostanzialmente riservato alle strutture pubbliche e alle strutture private accreditate e convenzionate con il Servizio Sanitario Nazionale, con un’attuazione fortemente disomogenea a livello regionale"; DB Medica (a practice-software vendor's blog, 20 Sep 2026, colour only): regional activation of channels for private structures still varies; Veneto Azienda Zero is still paying accredited private structures to reach FSE feeding targets, deadline moved to 30 May 2026 (https://www.azero.veneto.it/-/strutture-sanitarie-private-veneto). WRITE vs READ: the obligation is alimentazione (write); consultazione (read) is separate and consent-based. KIND OF PRIVATE: law covers accredited and authorised private structures incl. out-of-pocket care; gap is pure freelance practice and uneven regional activation. AGREEMENT WITH FILE: file ITA was partial on an Emilia-Romagna sentence; agrees, now on national evidence (law in force plus named gaps).

research.quote: 現在下記のスケジュールで、令和８年度冬頃に全国で利用可能な状態にすること（運用開始）を目指している。
research.source: 厚生労働省 政策統括官（情報政策担当）: 「医療DXの進捗状況等について（報告）」, 第130回社会保障審議会医療部会 資料１
research.notes: Translation: 'On the schedule below, we are aiming to make [the Electronic Health Record Information Sharing Service] usable nationwide (start of operation) around winter of fiscal 2026.' Same document: the service is still being verified in model projects in 10 regions ('現在、全国10地域でのモデル事業において、電子カルテ情報共有サービスの運用の検証や課題の確認などを進めている。'). Legal basis: MHLW paper on the 2025 Medical Care Act amendment bill (第115回社会保障審議会医療部会 資料１, 26 Feb 2025, https://www.mhlw.go.jp/content/12201000/001442574.pdf): '① 医療機関等は、３文書６情報を支払基金等に電子的に提供することができる旨を法律に位置づける。' (medical institutions MAY provide the 3 documents and 6 data items electronically) and '④ 地域医療支援病院等の管理者に３文書・６情報の共有に関する体制整備の努力義務を設ける。' (a duty to make efforts to set up sharing is placed only on managers of regional medical care support hospitals and similar). So participation is voluntary for ordinary clinics and hospitals and the service is not yet national. Why unknown rather than partial: Japanese hospitals and clinics are mostly privately owned but bill public health insurance, which is not 'private' under this brief; the private layer is self-pay care (自由診療, e.g. cosmetic, some dental). No ministry, operator or peer-reviewed source opened says whether 自由診療 episodes can or cannot be registered to the sharing service, and no source speaks of private-pay providers at all. The nationwide claims and eligibility links (オンライン資格確認, レセプト, マイナ保険証) are insurer/claims links and are excluded. Silence is unknown. Existing country file class: unknown; this research keeps unknown but adds the 2026 schedule and the voluntary legal footing.

research.quote: A data controller shall transmit health data containing sensitive personal data to the national health information data bank and county health information data bank in a secure and encrypted form.
research.source: Kenya Law (National Council for Law Reporting), Digital Health Act, 2023 (No. 15 of 2023), section 26(4)
research.notes: English source. Class unknown because no opened primary source has an operative sentence that names private providers with a duty to write to the shared health record or the data banks. What was checked: (1) Digital Health Act 2023 s.26(4) (quoted) puts the transmit duty on 'a data controller' without saying private; the Act's s.2 defines 'private health services' as 'provision of health services by a health facility that is not owned by the national or county governments and includes health care services provided by individuals, faith-based organizations, non-governmental organizations and private for profit health institutions', and s.21(2)(g) lets the Cabinet Secretary 'require all health data controllers and processors to report designated health data', so private facilities are within the Act's scope, but applying s.26(4) to them is an inference, not a sentence. (2) Digital Health (Health Information Management Procedures) Regulations, LN 76 of 2025, https://new.kenyalaw.org/akn/ke/act/ln/2025/76/eng@2025-04-11 (gazetted 2025-04-11): defines 'health facility' as 'the whole or part of a public or private institution', but the duty attached is certification, reg. 37(1): 'A healthcare provider or a health facility shall not use a digital health solution in the provision of healthcare services, unless the digital health solution has been certified by the Agency.' Reg. 16 gives a legacy-data migration duty (24 months after County Health Data Banks are operational); no ongoing feed duty naming private facilities was found. (3) Ministry of Health, 'Government Scales Up Digital Health Reform to Drive Accountability and Efficiency', 2025-06-16/18, https://www.health.go.ke/government-scales-digital-health-reform-drive-accountability-and-efficiency : 'The Comprehensive Integrated Health Information System is now operational in 17 counties' and 'The Afya Yangu platform now enables portability of patient data across health facilities.' No mention of private facilities. (4) SHA directive, Citizen Digital 2026-06-30, https://citizen.digital/article/sha-gives-hospitals-3-months-for-digital-integration-of-provider-panel-n385514 : 'Within the next three months, I expect all providers to be fully integrated. If not, we will have no option but to deconstruct non-compliant facilities' (SHA CEO). This is the insurer's HMIS/claims integration (real-time verification, electronic claims), which the brief excludes as a private-provider record link; noted only. Vendor and LinkedIn pages assert a 1 September 2026 deadline for all private facilities to run a DHA-certified HMIS integrated with the HIE; not opened as primary, not citable. Read access: Afya Yangu/SHR patient app exists (DHA), not evidence of private write. Agrees with the existing class in the country file (unknown).

research.quote: 보건복지부는 진료정보교류 사업에 참여하는 의료기관이 1만332곳으로, 사업 시작 후 처음으로 1만곳을 돌파했다고 12일 밝혔다.
research.source: Yonhap News (연합뉴스), 김잔디: '병원 옮겨도 진료기록은 이어져…정보교류 참여 의료기관 1만곳', reporting a Ministry of Health and Welfare announcement
research.notes: Translation: 'The Ministry of Health and Welfare said on the 12th that the number of medical institutions taking part in the health information exchange (진료정보교류) project is 10,332, passing 10,000 for the first time since the project began.' Same article: '사업에 참여하는 기관은 1만곳을 넘겼으나 컴퓨터단층촬영(CT)·자기공명영상(MRI) 등 영상정보까지 공유할 수 있는 의료기관은 약 600곳에 불과하다.' (participating institutions passed 10,000 but only about 600 can share imaging such as CT and MRI). Participation is voluntary and exchange is consent-based: '사업에 참여하는 병원들은 환자 동의하에 진료기록과 과거병력, 투약 내역 등을 교류한다.' Definitional note: almost every Korean hospital and clinic is privately owned but must bill the National Health Insurance Service (당연지정제), so by this brief's definition they are the grey-zone kind of private (privately owned, publicly billed). Care paid outside the scheme (비급여) happens inside those same institutions; no source was found that says whether 비급여 episodes are or are not included in the exchanged 진료기록요약지. Write vs read: participating institutions write referral, discharge and summary documents to the exchange; non-participating institutions write nothing; no total count of Korean medical institutions was opened, so the share is not stated here, but the ministry itself frames participation as still needing to spread ('진료정보교류 사업을 의료현장 전반에 확산') and says only about 600 institutions can share imaging. NHIS/HIRA claims data and the 건강정보 고속도로 patient-held app are insurer/claims or patient-shared views and are not counted. Second source: MOHW via korea.kr press release 9 Dec 2022, https://www.korea.kr/news/pressReleaseView.do?newsId=156541637 , title '모든 상급종합병원과 전국 7,500여 개 의료기관이 함께하는 진료정보교류 사업 성과공유회 개최' (all tertiary hospitals and about 7,500 institutions nationwide take part). Only some providers connect, so partial. Existing country file class: unknown; this research gives partial, with the caveat that the 'private' here is privately owned and publicly billed.

research.quote: Folgende Berufssparten sind als zur Datenspeicherung verpflichtete Gesundheitsdienstleistende an das eGD angebunden: Ärzte, Apotheker, Alters- und Pflegeheime, Chiropraktoren und Labors.
research.source: Landtag des Fürstentums Liechtenstein, Kleine Anfrage 'Akzeptanz und Nutzung elektronisches Gesundheitsdossier (eGD)' by Dagmar Bühler-Nigsch, answer by Regierungsrat Emanuel Schädler
research.notes: Translation: 'The following professional groups are connected to the eGD as health service providers obliged to store data: doctors, pharmacists, old-age and nursing homes, chiropractors and laboratories.' Next sentence: 'Von diesen nutzen derzeit insgesamt 126 angeschlossene Gesundheitsdienstleistende das System für die Erstellung, Übermittlung und Einsicht von behandlungsrelevanten Dokumenten.' (Of these, 126 connected providers currently use the system to create, transmit and view treatment documents.) Question dated 4 March 2026, answer 6 March 2026. Legal basis, licence-based with no payer condition: Gesetz über das elektronische Gesundheitsdossier (EGDG), LGBl. 2021 Nr. 213, Fassung 01.02.2026, https://www.gesetze.li/konso/2021213000, Art. 2 Abs. 1 Bst. c defines 'EGD-Gesundheitsdienstleister' as the Landesspital, the Alters- und Krankenhilfe, other Einrichtungen des Gesundheitswesens, '4. Ärzte, auch bei Ausübung ihres Berufes im Rahmen einer Ärztegesellschaft; 5. Apotheker, Chiropraktoren und Zahnärzte ...', i.e. all licensed doctors, whether or not they hold an OKP admission (patients of non-OKP doctors pay privately). Art. 19 Abs. 2: 'Ab dem 1. Juli 2023 sind EGD-Gesundheitsdienstleister verpflichtet: a) im Behandlungsfall die in Art. 5 Abs. 2 genannten Daten im elektronischen Gesundheitsdossier zu speichern' (referral letters, doctor reports, discharge reports, lab and imaging findings, medications). Kind of private: all ambulatory doctors in Liechtenstein are private practitioners; those without an OKP contract are the privately paid tier and are covered by the same duty. Caveats: the dossier exists for OKP-insured persons; neither source gives an upload-compliance rate or separates OKP from non-OKP doctors (126 is a count of connected providers); the country file already notes compliance was not verified. Write, not read. Country file class was unknown; moves to connected.

research.quote: Tądien įsigalioja pernai gruodį Seimo priimtas Sveikatos priežiūros įstaigų įstatymo pakeitimas, įpareigojantis teikiant su sveikatinimo veikla susijusias paslaugas privalomai naudotis Valstybės elektronine sveikatos paslaugų ir bendradarbiavimo infrastruktūros informacine sistema (ESPBI IS), paprastai vadinama e. sveikatos sistema. Gydymo įstaigoms, kurios ir toliau nesinaudos e. sveikatos sistema pacientų sveikatos duomenims tvarkyti, gali būti ribojamos arba stabdomos licencijos.
research.source: E. sveikata portal (esveikata.lt, run by Registrų centras, the main processor of ESPBI IS), news item: SAM primena: nuo rugsėjo 1-osios visos šalies gydymo įstaigos pacientų duomenis privalo tvarkyti e. sveikatos sistemoje
research.notes: Translation: 'On that day [1 September 2022] the amendment to the Law on Health Care Institutions adopted by the Seimas last December enters into force, obliging [institutions], when providing services related to health care activity, to use the State Electronic Health Services and Cooperation Infrastructure Information System (ESPBI IS), usually called the e-health system, on a mandatory basis. Treatment institutions that continue not to use the e-health system to manage patient health data may have their licences restricted or suspended.' Headline: 'nuo rugsėjo 1-osios visos šalies gydymo įstaigos pacientų duomenis privalo tvarkyti e. sveikatos sistemoje' (from 1 September all the country's treatment institutions must manage patient data in the e-health system). Page footer: 'Puslapis atnaujintas: 2022-08-17 2024-09-04' (published 2022-08-17, updated 2024-09-04). Scope: the duty sits in the Sveikatos priežiūros įstaigų įstatymas (Law on Health Care Institutions, I-1367, art. 45 duties of personal health care institutions) and is enforced through the institution's licence, so it attaches to licensing, not to a contract with the Valstybinė ligonių kasa; the headline says all institutions, and the sanction is licence restriction, which only makes sense for every licensed institution including private self-pay clinics. Limitation: the consolidated statute text itself could not be opened (e-tar.lt and infolex.lt return 403, e-seimas serves only the 1996 original as PDF and loads the current body by script), so the class rests on the operator's statement of the rule; a reviewer with access should confirm art. 45(1) point 4^1 wording. Earlier, participation was voluntary: the State Audit Office (Valstybės kontrolė, report 'Elektroninės sveikatos sistemos kūrimas') wrote that all institutions regardless of ownership 'gali naudotis' (may use) e-health services; the 2022 amendment turned this into a duty. No public source found naming a private-provider gap after September 2022; the November 2025 upgrade disruption in the country file is not ownership-specific. Kind of private: private clinics (privačios klinikos), whether or not they hold a VLK contract. Write (tvarkyti pacientų duomenis = manage patient data in the system), not read. Country file class was unknown; moves to connected.

research.quote: Un professionnel de santé, intervenant dans la prise en charge médicale du titulaire, détenteur d’une donnée qu’il estime utile et pertinente au sens de l’article 60quater, paragraphe 2 du Code de la sécurité sociale, verse celle-ci au dossier de soins partagé dans un délai raisonnable après la prise de connaissance de cette donnée ou après son premier accès au dossier de soins partagé si cette donnée est antérieure à son activation.
research.source: Journal officiel du Grand-Duché de Luxembourg, Mémorial A N° 909: Règlement grand-ducal du 6 décembre 2019 précisant les modalités et conditions de mise en place du dossier de soins partagé, Art. 9 (1)
research.notes: Translation: 'A health professional involved in the medical care of the holder, who holds a datum he considers useful and relevant within the meaning of article 60quater, paragraph 2 of the Social Security Code, deposits it in the shared care record within a reasonable time after becoming aware of it, or after his first access to the shared care record if the datum predates its activation.' Art. 9 (3) adds a 15-day limit after the end of care for lab results, clinical summaries and discharge reports, imaging reports etc. Scope is licence-based, not payer-based: Art. 1 5° defines 'Professionnel de santé' as 'toute personne physique exerçant légalement une profession réglementée du domaine de la santé et tout professionnel de santé, tout établissement hospitalier, ainsi que tout prestataire de soins, exerçant légalement sa profession en dehors du secteur hospitalier', and Art. 2 (5) speaks of the record each professional keeps 'quel que soit son mode d’exercice' (whatever his mode of practice). Landing page: https://legilux.public.lu/eli/etat/leg/rgd/2019/12/06/a909/jo (JavaScript-only; the PDF link above is the official file). Kind of private: in Luxembourg conventionnement with the CNS is compulsory for the regulated professions, so a purely non-conventioned private tier barely exists; the duty nonetheless attaches to legal exercise of the profession, so self-pay care (e.g. non-reimbursed services) by any legally practising professional falls under it. No source found naming a private-provider gap; the country file's gaps (low clinician use of the DSP, EU asking Luxembourg to speed up) are not ownership-specific, and the DSP is a summary layer ('ne se substitue pas au dossier que tient chaque professionnel'), not a full chart. Write, not read. Country file class was unknown; moves to connected.

research.quote: 45. Ārstniecības iestādēm ir pienākums tiešsaistē sniegt veselības informācijas sistēmai: 45.1. no 2016. gada 1. decembra – šo noteikumu 11.4.5. apakšpunktā norādītos datus; 45.2. no 2018. gada 1. janvāra – šo noteikumu 11.4.1., 11.4.2., 11.4.3., 11.4.6., 11.4.8., 11.4.9., 11.4.10. un 11.4.11. apakšpunktā norādītos datus, kā arī šo noteikumu 11.4.4. apakšpunktā norādītos datus, izrakstot zāles, kuru iegādes izdevumus pacientam daļēji vai pilnībā kompensē no valsts budžeta līdzekļiem.
research.source: Ministru kabinets (Cabinet of Ministers of Latvia), noteikumi Nr. 134 'Noteikumi par vienoto veselības nozares elektronisko informācijas sistēmu', point 45 (consolidated text on likumi.lv)
research.notes: Translation: '45. Medical treatment institutions have a duty to supply online to the health information system: 45.1. from 1 December 2016 the data in sub-point 11.4.5; 45.2. from 1 January 2018 the data in sub-points 11.4.1, 11.4.2, 11.4.3, 11.4.6, 11.4.8, 11.4.9, 11.4.10 and 11.4.11 [outpatient records, discharge summaries, sick-leave certificates, lab results, referrals etc.], as well as the data in 11.4.4 when prescribing medicines whose cost is partly or fully compensated from the state budget.' Date given is the consolidated redaction in force (08.08.2026); the regulation was adopted 11.03.2014 and took effect 01.04.2014. Scope is registration-based, not payer-based: Ārstniecības likums 1. pants 3) defines 'ārstniecības iestādes; ārstu prakses, valsts un pašvaldību iestādes, saimnieciskās darbības veicēji un komercsabiedrības, kas reģistrētas ārstniecības iestāžu reģistrā ...' (https://likumi.lv/ta/id/44108-arstniecibas-likums), so private commercial practices without an NVD contract are covered. Second source (news quoting the National Health Service): nra.lv, 4 Jul 2016, https://nra.lv/latvija/177351-pacienti-e-veseliba-pieslegties-vel-nevar.htm: 'No 2016. gada 1. decembra e-veselības sistēma būs obligāti jāsāk lietot visām ārstniecības iestādēm un aptiekām, neatkarīgi no tā, vai tās sniedz valsts vai privāti apmaksātus pakalpojumus, norāda Nacionālā veselības dienesta (NVD) speciāliste Evija Štālberga.' (From 1 December 2016 all medical institutions and pharmacies must start using e-veselība, regardless of whether they provide state-paid or privately paid services, says NVD specialist Evija Štālberga.) Third: LV portāls explainer 2026 (https://lvportals.lv/skaidrojumi/388343-kadi-dati-pieejami-e-veselibas-sistema-un-kas-tiem-var-pieklut-2026): 'sistēmā tiek uzglabāti arī rezultāti analīzēm, kas veiktas pēc pacienta iniciatīvas, pašam apmaksājot pakalpojumu' (the system also stores results of tests done on the patient's initiative and paid by the patient). Kind of private: self-pay and privately insured care at registered institutions; the duty attaches to registration in the medical institutions register. No source found naming a private-provider gap; the general gap in the country file (structured patient summary rarely filled) is not ownership-specific. Write, not read. Country file class was unknown; moves to connected.

research.quote: Por otro lado, existe la problemática que afecta a los sistemas de información de los integrantes del SNS, respecto a que no cumplen los estándares mínimos para intercambiar información nominal de la o el paciente; carentes de la desagregación de datos por sexo, edad, etnicidad y otros determinantes de la salud, repercute directamente en la capacidad para generar registros integrales y de calidad, afectando tanto a los servicios públicos como al sector privado, comprometiendo la integración de información de primera mano que incide en la toma de decisiones para la salud.
research.source: Diario Oficial de la Federación / Secretaría de Salud, PROGRAMA Sectorial de Salud 2025-2030 (section 5, Diagnóstico de la situación actual)
research.notes: Translation: 'On the other hand, there is the problem affecting the information systems of the members of the SNS [Sistema Nacional de Salud], in that they do not meet the minimum standards for exchanging patient-level (nominal) information; lacking disaggregation by sex, age, ethnicity and other health determinants, this bears directly on the capacity to produce complete, good-quality records, affecting both public services and the private sector, and compromising the integration of first-hand information that feeds health decision-making.' The SNS by law (Ley General de Salud art. 5) comprises public, social and private providers, so the sentence states that the systems of public and private members cannot exchange patient-level data. Supporting sentences on the same page: 'Ausencia de un Expediente Clínico Electrónico (ECE) Homologado: La falta de un ECE oficial y estandarizado a nivel nacional genera una dispersión de registros y duplicidad de información.' ('Absence of a harmonised ECE: the lack of an official, standardised national ECE produces a dispersion of records and duplication of information'); 'El hecho de que múltiples sistemas y bases de datos operen de manera independiente genera duplicidad de registros y la pérdida de información relevante en el historial del paciente.'; the 2023 SECE diagnostic 'A nivel nacional, solo el 36.32% de las unidades médicas han adoptado SECE'; and private as a 2030 goal only: 'El expediente clínico electrónico está completamente implementado en todos los niveles del sistema, tanto público como privado.' Kind of private: the whole private sector (private hospitals, consultorios adyacentes a farmacias, médicos particulares), paid out of pocket or by private insurance; Mexico has no contracted-private grey zone of note today. Write vs read: there is no national record for anyone to write to; each public institution keeps its own SECE. Second source, the shared record now being built: DOF 2026-04-17, DECRETO por el que se crea el Servicio Universal de Salud del Gobierno de México, https://dof.gob.mx/nota_detalle.php?codigo=5785257&fecha=17/04/2026 : the SUS is 'mecanismo obligatorio de coordinación e integración operativa entre las instituciones públicas federales que prestan servicios de salud' (Art. Primero), composed of IMSS, ISSSTE, IMSS-BIENESTAR, PEMEX, Hospitales Federales de Referencia, Institutos Nacionales de Salud/CCINSHAE and adhering state services (Art. Segundo), and its clinical information 'será compartida e intercambiada ... entre las instituciones de salud que integran el SUS' (Art. Octavo); private providers are not among them (silence on the decree's part, recorded as such). First exchange stage starts 2027-01-01. Presidencia press release 2026-01-20 on the credencial (https://www.gob.mx/presidencia/prensa/del-2-de-marzo-al-31-de-diciembre-se-realizara-credencializacion-del-servicio-universal-de-salud-presidenta-claudia-sheinbaum) names only IMSS, ISSSTE, IMSS Bienestar, Fuerzas Armadas and Institutos Nacionales de Salud; the credential is a read instrument ('acceso al expediente clínico electrónico'). Law: Ley General de Salud reform, DOF 2026-01-15 (https://dof.gob.mx/2026/PRESREP/PRESREP_150126_02.pdf), Art. 13 B V, obliges state governments to 'Integrar una base de datos con información estadística local alimentada por los prestadores de servicios de atención a la salud, tanto públicos como privados, con información nominal de la prestación de sus servicios': a statistical reporting database, not a clinical record. NOM-024-SSA3-2012 (DOF 2012-11-30, https://dof.gob.mx/nota_detalle.php?codigo=5280847&fecha=30/11/2012) is 'de observancia obligatoria ... para todos los establecimientos que presten servicios de atención médica que formen parte del Sistema Nacional de Salud que adopten un Sistema de Información de Registro Electrónico para la Salud': a software-system standard (the vendor trap in the brief), not a shared record. A PAN bill of 2026-09-22 (SIL, not in force) would let private institutions take part 'de manera complementaria y excepcional'; a draft, so it changes nothing. Agrees with the existing country-file class (split: 'Each institution (IMSS, ISSSTE, IMSS-Bienestar, private) keeps its own record today.').

research.quote: Nigeria’s healthcare system is highly fragmented; public hospitals, private clinics, pharmacies, and laboratories often operate in silos with minimal data exchange.
research.source: Health Economics Review (Springer/BMC), 'Beyond seed funding: why Nigerian digital health startups struggle to grow', doi 10.1186/s13561-025-00708-6, PMC12797844
research.notes: English source, peer-reviewed. Class split because the sentence names public hospitals and private clinics and says they operate in silos with minimal data exchange, i.e. records are not linked. Weakest of the six classes: the sentence is hedged ('often', 'minimal'); the paper is about startup financing and gives this as system context, not as an audit of record linkage. Kind of private: private clinics, pharmacies and laboratories generally (Nigeria has no national EHR, so there is no shared public record for private care to be written into). Context opened: Health Reporters, 2025-11-20, https://healthreporters.info/fg-advances-digital-health-financing-to-boost-uhc/ : 'He said that 7.2 million Nigerians were now registered on the National Health Information Exchange' and 'Salako said more than 200 hospitals had adopted Electronic Medical Record (EMR) systems' (Minister of State for Health at the 66th National Council on Health); neither says anything about private facilities feeding it. Premium Times, 2026-07-28, https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-news/898831-nigerian-govt-unveils-blueprint-for-secure-interoperable-digital-health-system.html : principles 'would guide the development of health information exchanges', so the exchange is still in development. NDHI site (https://www.digitalhealth.gov.ng/) lists a national EMR and data exchange as aspirations (720+ facilities to be digitised) with no statement on private facilities. PLOS Digital Health review (PMC11398640, 2024): 'Private facilities were however not included in any of the primary studies'. Existing class in the country file: unknown (file said facilities keep their own records and there is no national exchange, without naming private providers). This research moves it to split. [EDITOR FLAG: weakest class here: one hedged sentence ("often", "minimal") giving context in a startup-financing paper, not an audit. Nigeria has no national EHR for private care to feed.]
research.editorRuling: JAS-delegated 1 Oct 2026: unknown; one hedged sentence from a startup-financing paper is not enough evidence.

research.quote: De verplichtingen die bij of krachtens deze wet gelden omvatten in ieder geval niet de verplichting tot het uitwisselen van gegevens.
research.source: Overheid.nl (wetten.overheid.nl), Wet elektronische gegevensuitwisseling in de zorg (Wegiz), artikel 1.7, text in force from 2025-07-05
research.notes: Translation of the quote: 'The obligations that apply under or pursuant to this Act in any case do not include an obligation to exchange data.' Definition first: Dutch basic insurance (Zvw) is compulsory private insurance; under the brief, GPs, hospitals and insurer-contracted zelfstandige behandelcentra (ZBCs) that bill the Zvw are not 'private'. The brief's 'private' sector in the Netherlands is care paid outside the Zvw/Wlz (niet-verzekerde zorg, e.g. cosmetic clinics, self-pay). No public source found that says whether such providers write to, or make their records retrievable through, the national infrastructure (Landelijk Schakelpunt, LSP) or patients' persoonlijke gezondheidsomgevingen (PGO), so the class is unknown. Why the law does not settle it: the Wegiz (in force 2023-07-01, Stb. 2023, 135, https://zoek.officielebekendmakingen.nl/stb-2023-135.html: 'Met dit koninklijk besluit wordt het tijdstip van inwerkingtreding van de Wet elektronische gegevensuitwisseling in de zorg (hierna: Wegiz) vastgesteld op 1 juli 2023, met uitzondering van artikel 7.3') binds every 'zorgaanbieder' as defined in the Wkkgz, whatever the funding, but art. 2.1(1) only requires that a designated exchange, when it happens, runs over an electronic infrastructure ('Een zorgaanbieder ziet er op toe dat in een aangewezen gegevensuitwisseling bij het uitwisselen van gegevens door onder hem ressorterende zorgverleners ten minste gebruik wordt gemaakt van een elektronische infrastructuur.'), and art. 1.7 (the quote) says it creates no duty to exchange at all; so it is not a rule requiring private providers to feed a shared record. Ministry wording, VWS datavoorgezondheid.nl/onderwerpen/w/wegiz (undated): 'In de Wegiz staat dat gegevensuitwisseling tussen zorgaanbieders in sommige gevallen elektronisch moet verlopen.' Designated exchanges so far: GP prescription to pharmacy, in force 2024-01-01 (Stb. 2023, 370, https://zoek.officielebekendmakingen.nl/stb-2023-370.html); the Basisgegevensset Zorg between medisch-specialistische-zorg institutions, which the hospital association NVZ's implementation guide (April 2025, https://www.nvz-ziekenhuizen.nl/sites/default/files/2025-06/Handreiking%20BgZ%20implementatie%20%20v1.0.pdf) says 'wordt verplicht onder de Wet elektronische gegevensuitwisseling in de zorg (Wegiz) per 2027' and 'Vanaf 1 januari 2027 treedt deze verplichting in werking en zijn instellingen voor medisch specialistische zorg wettelijk gebonden om aan de eisen te voldoen' (that AMvB's publication was not verified in this pass). The LSP is not a record but a retrieval network and joining is voluntary: VZVZ/Volgjezorg FAQ (undated), https://www.volgjezorg.nl/veelgestelde-vragen/over-het-lsp : 'Zorgaanbieders bepalen zelf of zij willen aansluiten op het Landelijk Schakelpunt.' ('Care providers decide for themselves whether they want to connect to the LSP'). Grey zone (insurer-contracted independent clinics): NVZ guide, 'LSP (Landelijk Schakelpunt): Veel gebruikt door zelfstandige klinieken en categorale instellingen.' ('LSP: much used by independent clinics and specialised institutions'); ZKN (independent clinics association) news 2025-10-10, https://www.zkn.nl/nieuws/4704-is-uw-zkn-kliniek-klaar-voor-de-bgz-msz-uitwisseling : 'De verplichting tot elektronische BgZ-uitwisseling in de msz komt eraan.' If the owner accepts contracted ZBCs as 'private', these sentences would read as partial (some connect; a 2027 deadline). Write vs read: LSP participants make their own records retrievable (write side) and query others (read side); there is no national EHR. Agrees with the existing country-file class (unknown, silent).

research.quote: Tilgang til dokumenter fra private aktører, slik som avtalespesialister, private bildediagnostiske sentre og laboratorier, nevnes av over halvparten av intervjuobjektene.
research.source: Helsedirektoratet (Norwegian Directorate of Health), report: Foreløpig evaluering av nytte og utfordringer, for videre innføring av pasientens journaldokumenter, chapter 3.1 Behov for dokumentdeling
research.notes: Translation: 'Access to documents from private actors, such as contract specialists, private imaging centres and laboratories, is mentioned [as missing] by over half of the interviewees.' The same chapter quotes a GP: 'Savner mye mer fra de helprivate (de sender ikke epikriser i det hele tatt).' (I miss much more from the fully private ones; they do not send discharge summaries at all.) Kind of private: both avtalespesialister (publicly contracted, grey zone) and helprivate clinics (fully private); neither publishes documents to Pasientens journaldokumenter today. Second source, the operator's own list of who shares documents, NHN 'Hvem har tilgang til hva?' (https://www.nhn.no/tjenester/pasientens-journaldokumenter/hvem-har-tilgang-til-tjenesten, undated): 'Dele journaldokumenter: Sykehusene i Helse Nord ... Sykehusene i Helse Sør-Øst ... Lovisenberg ... Sykehusene i Helse Vest ... Oslo kommune med behandlingsstedene; Oslo legevakt, Observasjonsposten og Kommunal akutt døgnenhet (KAD)', no private provider listed. NHN roadmap (https://www.nhn.no/tjenester/pasientens-journaldokumenter/veikart, 'Sist oppdatert: 12. mar. 2026'): 'Avtalespesialister skal dele journaldokumenter Helseforetakene pågår ukjent' (contract specialists to share documents: in progress, date unknown). Not split: dispensed prescriptions are shared nationally regardless of prescriber; Helsenorge, 'Om helseopplysninger som deles' (https://www.helsenorge.no/helseopplysninger-som-deles/om/, undated): 'Følgende opplysninger knyttet til resepter og legemidler er tilgjengelig for helsepersonell: Legemidler du har fått utlevert på resept i norske apotek' and, on documents, 'Helsepersonell kan se dine journaldokumenter fra sykehus.' The gap is in documents, not prescriptions. Write (publishing documents) not read; read access via kjernejournal is national. Country file class was unknown; moves to partial.

research.quote: radiology reports (hospital imaging and private reports copied to the system)
research.source: Health New Zealand | Te Whatu Ora, TestSafe (guidance for health professionals)
research.notes: English, no translation needed. Sub-national: TestSafe is the Auckland and Northland regional clinical data repository ("It is used across Auckland and Northland in hospitals and the community."); the quote is one list item under "Depending on your role, TestSafe can show:". WRITE: private radiology reports are copied into the regional record, one document type only; NZ radiology practices are private businesses that are often also publicly contracted, so a grey zone. READ: the same page lists "some specialists and private providers (by application)." among authorised users; that is read access only. National picture: the Shared Digital Health Record page (Health NZ, last updated 7 August 2026, https://www.healthnz.govt.nz/privacy/wider-sharing-of-your-health-information/privacy-shared-digital-health-record ) names its sources as "general practice, urgent care and telehealth services (medical practices)" and "some national Health NZ databases", says "Sharing of this information will not start until 2027.", and names no private hospital or private specialist source; the 64-page SDHR privacy impact assessment does not mention private providers. That silence is left as silence, not read as split. NZ general practices are privately owned but publicly capitated, so they are not "private" for this layer. Existing class in the country file: unknown. This changes it to partial.

research.source: Department of Health (Philippines), Health Policy Development and Planning Bureau: 'National Objectives for Health Philippines 2023-2028' (copy hosted by the Philippine Academy of Family Physicians; DOH says the electronic copy is at www.doh.gov.ph / hpdpbplanning.doh.gov.ph)
research.notes: English source. Full passage (p. 47): 'The Philippines has invested considerably in digital health with 88 percent of its public primary care facilities using electronic medical records (EMRs). However, according to the PHFDP, 59 percent of private primary care facilities remain without EMRs. Sixty-three out of seventy DOH-retained hospitals are implementing telemedicine, but data from private health providers are not yet included in the report.' Indicator on p. 2169 of the text: 'Percent of health facilities utilizing interoperable electronic medical records for digitalized service delivery / Baseline: TBD / 2028 Target: 100%'. Kind of private: privately owned hospitals and primary care clinics, which in the Philippines deliver most care and are paid by PhilHealth benefits plus large out-of-pocket shares; the law does not distinguish by payer. RULE IN FORCE: Republic Act 11223 (Universal Health Care Act, 2019), Section 36, https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2019/ra_11223_2019.html : 'All health service providers and insurers shall each maintain a health information system consisting of enterprise resource planning, human resource information, electronic health records, and an electronic prescription log consistent with DOH standards, which shall be electronically uploaded on a regular basis through interoperable systems'. IRR (10 Oct 2019) s.36.1 repeats it with 'standards set by the DOH and PhilHealth'. Write vs read: the obligation is to upload; the designated destination is the National Health Data Repository run by PhilHealth with DOH (RA 11223 s.31, JAO 2021-0002), which is a national data repository rather than a point-of-care record, and PhilHealth is also the insurer, so the exclusion rule for claims links applies in part. No national clinical exchange is operational: Zuniga et al., Frontiers in Digital Health, 30 Jan 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12915754/ : 'In the Philippines, early efforts to establish a national HIE began in 2015 with the Philippine Health Information Exchange (PHIE), but infrastructure limitations, governance challenges, and uneven digital readiness constrained progress.' Rule in force covers private providers; DOH itself names the private gap (59% of private primary care facilities without EMRs, private hospital data not in its report) and sets a 2028 target, so partial. Existing country file class: unknown; this research gives partial.

research.quote: Raportowanie zdarzeń medycznych jest obowiązkiem wszystkich podmiotów medycznych niezależnie od tego, czy świadczenia są udzielane w ramach kontraktu z NFZ, czy komercyjnie.
research.source: Centrum e-Zdrowia (national e-health operator, runs the P1 system), 'e-zdrowie w liczbach: zdarzenia medyczne'
research.notes: Translation: 'Reporting medical events is an obligation of all medical entities regardless of whether services are provided under an NFZ contract or commercially.' Kind of private: fully commercial (out-of-pocket / private insurance) providers with no NFZ contract, as well as private practices; the operator names both. Write, not read: the obligation is to transmit (przekazywać) medical-event data to SIM/P1, i.e. a write. Rule in force: ustawa z 28 kwietnia 2011 o systemie informacji w ochronie zdrowia, art. 56 ust. 2a: 'Usługodawcy są obowiązani przekazywać do SIM dane zdarzenia medycznego przetwarzanego w systemie informacji od dnia 1 lipca 2021 r.' ('Service providers are obliged to transmit to SIM the data of a medical event processed in the information system from 1 July 2021'); art. 2 pkt 15 defines usługodawca as the świadczeniodawca of art. 5 pkt 41 of the 2004 public-financing act plus pharmacies, i.e. any entity performing medical activity, contract or not (consolidated text Kancelaria Sejmu, t.j. Dz.U. 2026 poz. 208, https://api.sejm.gov.pl/eli/acts/DU/2011/657/text/U/D20110657Lj.pdf). Second supporting source, dated: CeZ news 11.02.2025 'Już ponad miliard zdarzeń medycznych zgłoszonych do e-zdrowia' (http://www.cez.gov.pl/pl/page/o-nas/aktualnosci/juz-ponad-miliard-zdarzen-medycznych-zgloszonych-do-e-zdrowia): 'każdy lekarz lub placówka medyczna od 1 lipca 2021 roku mają obowiązek raportowania zdarzeń medycznych w systemie e-zdrowie – także wówczas, gdy ktoś leczy się prywatnie.' ('every doctor or medical facility has had a duty since 1 July 2021 to report medical events in the e-health system, also when someone is treated privately'); the same page reports 982 mln NFZ-funded events plus 184 mln 'za które pacjenci zapłacili prywatnie' (paid privately) in P1, so private care is demonstrably written to the shared record. Gap check (not private-specific): the same CeZ page adds 'Część podmiotów nie wypełnia tego obowiązku' ('Some entities do not fulfil this duty'); CeZ IX informatization survey, August 2026, data for 2025 (http://www.cez.gov.pl/sites/default/files/paragraph.attachments.field_attachments/2026-08/Raport%20z%20Badania%20stopnia%20informatyzacji%20PWDL%20za%202025.pdf): 'Najwyższy wskaźnik raportowania wykazują podmioty szpitalne (79,2%), a najniższy AŚZ (62,6%).' (highest reporting rate among hospital entities 79.2%, lowest among ambulatory entities 62.6%); the survey splits by facility type, not by public/private ownership, and I found no CeZ or NIK figure on private-provider compliance specifically. Trade press names a private gap: Rynek Zdrowia 3 Jul 2025 (https://www.rynekzdrowia.pl/E-zdrowie/Niemal-polowa-podmiotow-leczniczych-zagrozona-Rzad-szykuje-kary,273095,7.html): 'obowiązek raportowania zdarzeń medycznych ignoruje dziś wiele prywatnych podmiotów' ('many private entities ignore the reporting duty today') and reports a planned NFZ financing sanction from 1 Jan 2026 that 'obejmie tylko placówki mające umowę z NFZ' (covers only NFZ-contracted facilities); I did not verify enactment of that sanction (ISAP is bot-blocked). Ruling: the only private-specific gap statement found is that unsourced assertion in trade press; every primary measure (operator page, CeZ 11.02.2025, CeZ IX survey 2026) splits by facility type, not ownership, and the brief ranks primary sources over news, so connected stands on the rule in force and the operator's statement. Flip condition: a CeZ or NIK figure on private-provider compliance would move this to partial; I searched for one (CeZ VIII and IX survey reports, NIK result pages) and found none. The class page carries no article date; its footer reads © 2026 Centrum e-Zdrowia. Agrees with the existing country-file class (connected).

research.quote: Os dados serão integrados e partilhados com os prestadores públicos, mesmo que não usem sistemas de informação da SPMS, e com os prestadores privados e do setor social que utilizem sistemas de informação em conformidade com os serviços do RSEu.
research.source: SPMS (Serviços Partilhados do Ministério da Saúde, EPE), "Registo de Saúde Eletrónico Único determina futuro da saúde pública"
research.notes: Translation: "Data will be integrated and shared with public providers, even if they do not use SPMS information systems, and with private and social-sector providers that use information systems compliant with the RSEu services." Future tense: the Registo de Saúde Eletrónico Único (RSEu) is under development, steered by a working group created by Despacho n.º 3030/2025 de 7 de março with 22 public, private and social-sector entities; the same page requires "Certificação obrigatória das soluções aplicacionais ... antes da integração no RSEu". SECOND SOURCE: Público 11 Jul 2024 (updated 12 Jul 2024), quoting SPMS: "os tempos de implementação do Registo de Saúde Electrónico (RSEu) pelos prestadores dos sectores privado e social é uma decisão dos mesmos, sendo que o Regulamento do Espaço Europeu de Dados de Saúde determina 2028 como data limite" (https://www.publico.pt/2024/07/11/sociedade/noticia/ministra-saude-partilha-dados-doentes-privados-so-autorizacao-utente-2097073); the minister said sharing with privates happens only with the patient's authorisation and a pilot with the CUF group was starting. READ ACCESS, separately: SPMS 2020 "Registo de Saúde Eletrónico – Área do Profissional disponível nos setores privado e social": a doctor in the private or social sector "pode obter informação clínica" in the RSE professional area (view only) (https://www.spms.min-saude.pt/2020/01/registo-de-saude-eletronico-area-do-profissional-disponivel-nos-setores-privado-e-social/). JN 25 Nov 2022, SPMS president on RSE: "há muita informação que ainda não está disponível". No law or despacho in force was found that requires private or social-sector providers to write to the RSE (DRE searched; Despacho 3030/2025 only creates the working group); the only deadline cited is the EHDS 2028 limit. KIND OF PRIVATE: all private and social-sector providers, including purely private ones; none currently writes to the shared record except through the pilot. Pages read via web.archive.org copies because spms.min-saude.pt and publico.pt block automated fetches; the quotes were checked against the archived page text. AGREEMENT WITH FILE: file PRT was partial ("Data held only by private providers is often missing."); agrees. [Parent re-check 2026-10-01: spms.min-saude.pt blocks automated fetches; quote rests on the research agent's Internet Archive copy.]

research.quote: Sistemul DES este un serviciu public furnizat de CNAS, pentru toţi pacienţii care, potrivit prevederilor titlului VIII, sunt asiguraţi ai sistemului de asigurări sociale de sănătate şi pentru toţi furnizorii de servicii medicale pe toate tipurile de asistenţă medicală, indiferent dacă se află sau nu în relaţie contractuală cu o casă de asigurări de sănătate. Acest serviciu urmează să fie utilizat gradual de la data implementării în sistemul DES a funcţionalităţilor specifice fiecărui tip de asistenţă medicală.
research.source: Parlamentul României, Legea nr. 45/2019 pentru modificarea şi completarea Legii nr. 95/2006 (inserts Titlul IX^1 'Dosarul electronic de sănătate al pacientului'), art. 346^5 alin. (1), as published on lege5.ro
research.notes: Translation: 'The DES system is a public service provided by CNAS, for all patients who under Title VIII are insured in the social health insurance system and for all providers of medical services across all types of medical care, whether or not they are in a contractual relationship with a health insurance house. This service is to be used gradually from the date the functionalities specific to each type of care are implemented in the DES.' Published in Monitorul Oficial nr. 192 of 11 March 2019, in force 14 March 2019. Same law, art. 346^9 (2): 'Înregistrarea şi transmiterea datelor şi informaţiilor medicale către sistemul DES sunt obligatorii pentru toţi furnizorii de servicii medicale, sub sancţiunea prevăzută la art. 346^10 alin. (2)-(4), fără a fi necesar consimţământul pacienţilor.' and art. 346^10 (3) sets contravention fines (3-5% of the value of untransmitted services) for 'furnizorii de servicii medicale care nu se află în relaţie contractuală cu o casă de asigurări de sănătate'. Kind of private: fully private providers and hospitals without a CNAS contract (self-pay or private insurance), explicitly covered. Why partial, not connected: the law itself says use is gradual, and the record is known to be thin: Sorana Stănescu, Foaia de observație, 31 May 2023 (https://sorana.substack.com/p/dosar-elecronic-de-sanatate): 'nici nu se actualizează automat de fiecare dată când mergi la o consultație „în privat”, deși ar trebui' (nor is it updated automatically each time you go to a private consultation, although it should be), and doctors told her the dossiers are 'atât de goale, încât sunt irelevante'. Presence of art. 346^5 confirmed in the CTCE consolidated Legea 95/2006 (form valid 03-11-2020, reposted at https://dm.mai.gov.ro/kretzulescu/legea-95-2006/). Write, not read. Country file class was unknown; moves to partial.

Earlier New Times piece (2025-01-17, article 23344) returned no body text. Claims that the Ministry plans to link e-Ubuzima with private clinics and pharmacies appear only on vendor/aggregator sites and social posts (toppingafrica, medsoftwares, Facebook posts quoting a 2027 national HIE); none is a citable primary and none was used. Ministry of Health pages opened (moh.gov.rw e-Ubuzima/NHIC news) do not mention private facilities. Agrees with the existing class in the country file (unknown: 'We did not verify whether private clinics or pharmacies are connected').

research.quote: In the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, the health care system consists of multiple isolated sectors, and there is a need for an overarching body coordinating data sets, indicators, and reports at the national level.
research.source: Metsallik et al., Journal of Medical Internet Research 26:e53369: 'Assessing Opportunities and Barriers to Improving the Secondary Use of Health Care Data at the National Level: Multicase Study in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and Estonia'
research.notes: English source. The paper describes fragmentation across government sectors and notes 'The private sector in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia runs 167 hospitals with 19,427 beds', but it does not say whether private hospitals write to any shared clinical record, so it settles nothing about private providers. Excluded by the brief: NPHIES (نفيس), the national platform for health and insurance information exchange, which the NHIC describes as linking providers and insurers and whose facility-connection index (https://nhic.gov.sa/nuc/) tracks insurer-related use cases; the Council of Health Insurance's 2021 mandate for private facilities to join it (chi.gov.sa news item, search snippet only, page not opened) is an insurer/claims link. The Saudi Health Information Exchange policies (NHIC IS0303, Saudi Health Council, version 1.0, 21 Apr 2016, https://nhic.gov.sa/standards/Policies/IS0303-Saudi-Health-Information-Exchange-Policies-v1.0.pdf) define a 'Covered Entity' as 'An entity that is required to abide by the Saudi Health Information Exchange Policy' and mention 'public and private hospitals' only in a registry definition; no clause opened requires private providers to feed a shared record. The NHIC's statutory task is 'التنسيق مع الجهات المعنية لإيجاد ملف صحي إلكتروني موحد لكل مريض' (coordinating with the relevant bodies to create a unified electronic health file for every patient), per the NHIC organisation regulation on laws.boe.gov.sa, which is a mandate to coordinate, not a rule on private providers (seen in search results; the page is JavaScript-rendered and was not opened). Kind of private that matters: private hospitals and clinics paid by mandatory private insurance for expatriates and private-sector employees, or out of pocket. No ministry, NHIC, Seha Virtual Hospital or peer-reviewed source opened says whether they write to a national clinical record outside NPHIES. Silence is unknown. Existing country file class: unknown; this research keeps unknown.

research.quote: Poskytnutá zdravotná starostlivosť na priamu úhradu sa neposiela do zdravotnej poisťovne v zúčtovacej dávke. Postup je v tomto prípade bez zmeny, zdravotný záznam má byť zapísaný do eZdravia aj v tomto prípade.
research.source: NCZI (Národné centrum zdravotníckych informácií), ezdravotnictvo.sk: FAQs eZapisovanie vo vzťahu k zdravotným poisťovniam (časť B), question B1-10
research.notes: Translation: 'Health care provided for direct payment is not sent to the health insurer in the billing batch. The procedure in this case is unchanged: the health record must be written into eZdravie in this case too.' The question it answers: 'Ako sa bude na zdravotnú poisťovňu vykazovať poskytnutie zdravotnej starostlivosti, ktoré si pacient hradil na priamu úhradu?' Page footer: 'aktualizované dňa 11. 09. 2026'. Kind of private: out-of-pocket (priama úhrada) care, which is how care at providers without an insurer contract is paid; the operator says such care must still be written to the national EZK. Legal basis (licence-based): Act 153/2013 Z. z. § 5, duty to write to the elektronická zdravotná knižka from 1.1.2018 for every poskytovateľ zdravotnej starostlivosti (defined in Act 578/2004 by povolenie/licencia, not by insurer contract). Second source: SSVPL / h&h Partners overview (https://ssvpl.sk/ezdravie-strucny-prehlad-povinnosti-poskytovatelov-zdravotnej-starostlivosti/): 'Povinnosť zapisovať údaje do knižky: od 1.1.2018' and 'Poskytovateľ ZS má povinnosť bezodkladne po poskytnutí ambulantnej zdravotnej starostlivosti vytvoriť záznam do EZK'. Caveats: the same FAQ phases in mandatory writing for day clinics (stacionáre) from 1.1.2027 and tissue banks from 1.7.2027, by provider type, not ownership; the 1 July 2026 rule tying insurer payment to the EZZ ID (Act 344/2025) is an insurer link and is NOT the basis for this class. Write, not read. Country file class was unknown; moves to connected.

research.quote: V prilogi pa ni predviden niti rok niti način vključitve in uporabe posamezne storitve eZdravja za zasebne izvajalce brez koncesije, pač pa so kot obvezni uporabniki določeni zgolj izvajalci zdravstvene dejavnosti v mreži javne zdravstvene službe.
research.source: Zdravniška zbornica Slovenije (Medical Chamber of Slovenia), notice: Odbor za zobozdravstvo obravnaval problematiko obveznega vključevanja zasebnih izvajalcev v zNET
research.notes: Translation: 'But the annex [to the Pravilnik o pogojih, rokih, načinu vključitve in uporabe eZdravja za obvezne uporabnike, Uradni list RS 69/15, 25/19, 10/21, 58/21] foresees neither a deadline nor a method of inclusion and use of individual eZdravje services for private providers without a concession; rather, only providers within the public health service network are designated as obligatory users.' The preceding sentence on the page states the law: ZZPPZ art. 14 'določa, da so obvezni uporabniki eZdravja vsi izvajalci zdravstvene dejavnosti, torej ni izrecne omejitve na izvajalce v mreži javne zdravstvene službe' (all providers are obligatory users, no limitation to the public network). Kind of private: zasebniki brez koncesije (self-pay private providers); koncesionarji are inside the public network and are not private for this layer. Supporting, more recent but without a deadline: Ministry of Health / NIJZ eZdravje support FAQ (undated, https://podpora.ezdrav.si/faq/ali-lahko-crpp-uporabljajo-tudi-zasebniki-brez-koncesije/): 'Da. V skladu z veljavno zakonodajo so izvajalci zdravstvene dejavnosti obvezni uporabniki eZdravja, zasebniki niso izvzeti. Tudi zasebniki brez koncesije lahko v CRPP posredujejo izvide ter pridobivajo podatke, ki so potrebni za zdravstveno obravnavo.' (Yes. Under current law providers are obligatory users of eZdravje; private providers are not exempt. Private providers without a concession can also submit findings to the CRPP and obtain data needed for treatment.) The Information Commissioner (IP-RS opinion 07121-1/2022/902, 18.08.2022) and the NIJZ May 2026 deck ('Sodelovati morajo vsi javni in zasebni izvajalci zdravstvenih storitev.') say the same. The operator FAQ thus says private providers are obligatory users and can submit; what it and every later source lack is a deadline or method for non-concession providers, which is exactly the gap the Chamber named. Searches surfaced no amendment to the rulebook after Uradni list 58/21 (PISRS itself is JavaScript-only and could not be opened), and the operator's CRPP page (https://ezdrav.si/resitve/crpp/) still cites the 69/15 rulebook as the basis of the sending duty, so the 2021 gap is not shown to be closed. The country file's general note that some providers do not send to CRPP is not ownership-specific. Write ('posredujejo izvide' = submit findings), not read. Country file class was unknown; moves to partial.

research.quote: 由於雲端系統所涵攝之雲端資訊，係由健保特約之各醫事服務機構，將其申報健保給付醫療費用所屬之相關醫療資訊上傳而來，加以健保鼓勵上傳醫療資訊方案，並未及於非健保事項之醫療資訊，致目前實務上，自費就診之非健保給付所屬醫療資訊，原則上不會上傳，而形成「醫療雲的缺角」。
research.source: 立法院 法制局 (Legislative Yuan, Legal Affairs Bureau), 謝碧珠: 專題研究 A01462「健保醫療雲端系統欠缺自費就診醫療資訊問題研究」
research.notes: Translation: 'Because the information held in the cloud system is uploaded by NHI-contracted medical service institutions from the medical information attached to the medical expenses they claim from the NHI, and the NHI incentive scheme for uploading medical information does not extend to medical information on non-NHI matters, in current practice the medical information from self-pay visits that is not covered by the NHI is in principle not uploaded, forming a missing corner of the medical cloud.' Kind of private: Taiwan's providers are almost all privately owned and 93% are NHI-contracted (existing country file), so by this brief's definition they are the grey-zone kind; the private layer is self-pay care (自費就診), both at contracted institutions and at the roughly 7% non-contracted ones. Write vs read: NHI MediCloud (健保醫療資訊雲端查詢系統) is fed from NHI claims submissions (申報) plus incentivised uploads of results and images; it is a claims-fed record, and the Legislative Yuan report says self-pay care is in principle not written to it. Later supporting source: China Medical University Hospital patient FAQ, 20 Apr 2026, https://www.cmuh.cmu.edu.tw/Question/Detail?no=19353 : '本院是依照健保署「全民健康保險鼓勵醫事服務機構即時查詢病患就醫資訊方案」公告需上傳的項目進行上傳作業，若是自費檢查有可能不會是需要規定上傳的項目裡' (the hospital uploads the items the NHIA scheme requires; self-pay tests may not be among the items required to be uploaded). Second source, primary and current: NHIA (衛生福利部中央健康保險署) FAQ for the cloud system, item '個人的健檢結果或自費做的各項檢查報告也有上傳至健保醫療資訊雲端查詢系統嗎?', https://www.nhi.gov.tw/ch/cp-7635-5e691-2727-1.html (published 112-05-18, updated 112-11-29, i.e. 18 May 2023 / 29 Nov 2023; the live page sits behind a JavaScript challenge, text copied from the Internet Archive copy at https://web.archive.org/web/2025/https://www.nhi.gov.tw/ch/cp-7635-5e691-2727-1.html): 'A：自108年7月起本系統新增病人同意醫療院所協助上傳之自費健康檢查資料。' (Since July 2019 the system has added self-pay health-check data that institutions upload with the patient's consent.) So one slice of self-pay care, health checks, can be written in with consent; other self-pay care is not required to be uploaded. Classed partial rather than split because the primary source frames self-pay care as a gap ('缺角') in an otherwise near-universal record, the gap is 'in principle' not absolute, the NHIA confirms a consent-based path for self-pay health checks since 2019, and the 2026 hospital answer confirms the rest of the gap persists. Existing country file class: unknown; this research gives partial.

research.quote: Інші медичні записи можуть вноситись до ЕСОЗ за рішенням закладу.
research.source: Електронна система охорони здоров'я (ehealth.gov.ua, the ESOZ operator's site), 'Розвіюємо міф: чи впливає наявність договору з НСЗУ на роботу закладу в ЕСОЗ?'
research.notes: Translation of the quote: 'Other medical records may be entered into ESOZ at the facility's discretion.' Same page, scope sentence: 'така вимога передбачена Ліцензійними умовами провадження медичної практики для усіх медзакладів, незалежно від їхньої форми власності – комунальні, приватні чи лікарі-ФОП' (this requirement [to register and work in ESOZ] is set by the Licensing Conditions for medical practice for all medical facilities regardless of ownership: municipal, private, or self-employed doctors). Same page: 'Навіть якщо ваш медичний заклад не співпрацює з НСЗУ, ви все одно маєте зареєструватися в системі' (even if your facility does not work with the NHSU you must still register in the system). The page lists what every licensee must enter regardless of an NHSU contract: birth and sick-leave conclusions, e-prescription records, reimbursed medical-device prescriptions, the encounter records those documents rest on, records/referrals/prescriptions for services under the Programme of Medical Guarantees or other state-funded programmes, referrals including neonatal screening, and rehabilitation records; then the quoted sentence makes every other record optional. Kind of private: this is about private FACILITIES and private practitioners (ФОП), not the private medical information system (MIS) vendors that the country file already excludes. Care at a private clinic paid by the NHSU under the Programme of Medical Guarantees must be recorded; for self-paid (out-of-pocket or private insurance) care only the listed document types are mandatory and the rest is at the clinic's discretion. That named gap is why the class is partial, not connected. Write, not read: the rule is a duty to register and enter records into the central database; the same page notes connected private clinics gain read access to the patient's full history with consent. Second source (legal basis, opened): Cabinet of Ministers Resolution No. 285 of 2 March 2016, Licensing Conditions for medical practice, para. 13 sub-paras 30 and 31 (added by Resolution No. 126 of 16 Feb 2022), https://zakon.rada.gov.ua/laws/show/285-2016-%D0%BF/print : '30) зареєструватися в Реєстрі суб'єктів господарювання у сфері охорони здоров'я центральної бази даних електронної системи охорони здоров'я;' and '31) забезпечити роботу з електронною системою охорони здоров'я, зокрема внесення первинної облікової медичної документації, ведення обліку медичних послуг, управління медичною інформацією та використання інших функціональних можливостей електронної системи охорони здоров'я, які визначені законодавством обов'язковими в процесі провадження господарської діяльності з медичної практики;' (register in the ESOZ business-entity register; ensure work with ESOZ, including entry of primary medical documentation, as far as the law makes it mandatory). The licence applies to all legal forms of ownership. Existing class in the country file: unknown (file only noted private MIS vendors and that completeness depends on what each clinic enters). This research moves it to partial.

research.quote: Participating non-VA partners and providers are organizations that have trusted agreements with VA for electronic health information exchange.
research.source: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Veterans Health Information Exchange (VHIE), 'How VHIE Works'
research.notes: English source. Definition first, because the United States has no national public health system: Medicare and Medicaid are payers with no clinical record, so the only public system that both delivers care and keeps a record is the Veterans Health Administration (VA), and this entry is scoped to it. 'Private' here = non-VA (community) providers, which are privately owned; most of the care they give to Veterans is paid by VA under the Community Care programme (the brief's grey zone, publicly funded care by private providers), and the same exchange also carries records of care Veterans pay for privately. Write vs read: VA's exchange is bi-directional, so participating community providers' documents flow into VA's record and VA's flow out. VA, 'Why Partner with VHIE', https://www.va.gov/VHIE/Why_Partner_with_VHIE.asp (last updated 2026-09-16): 'VA Exchange, powered by eHealth Exchange, Carequality, and CommonWell Health Alliance, enables bi-directional sharing of VA health information between VA and participating non-VA partners and providers.' and, on joining: 'For more information on how to participate, please see our VA Exchange Non-VA Provider Onboarding Flyer'. Why partial and not connected: participation rests on a trusted agreement and onboarding (the quote), VA keeps a state-by-state list of 'Participating Non-VA Partners and Providers' (https://www.va.gov/VHIE/VHIE_Participating_Partners.asp, last updated 2025-07-25), and the VA community-care page (https://department.va.gov/vha/community-care/care-coordination/care-coordination-tools/, undated) says 'VHIE enables bi-directional sharing of Veteran Health Information between the VA and participating community providers.' and 'If your hospital or health care system is interested in creating this connection, view the Veterans Health Information Exchange (VHIE) website.' No VA sentence found gives the share of community providers that participate; the gap is that only providers with an agreement connect, so 'only some private providers connect'. Nationwide: ONC's TEFCA page (https://www.healthit.gov/topic/interoperability/policy/trusted-exchange-framework-and-common-agreement-tefca) describes 'a nationwide framework for health information sharing', a network-of-networks, not a shared record that private providers write to; not used for the class. Caveat: this is a VA-scoped class; for the US population as a whole there is no public record to be written into, which the brief's classes do not capture. Existing country-file class was unknown (silent); this fresh evidence gives partial for the VA scope only. [EDITOR FLAG: scoped to the VA as the only public system that keeps a clinical record. Medicare and Medicaid are payers. Do not read this as a national class.]
research.editorRuling: JAS-delegated 1 Oct 2026: unknown; evidence covers the VA only, not a national class.
