research.source: Hội đồng phối hợp phổ biến, giáo dục pháp luật thành phố Cần Thơ (Can Tho city government legal-dissemination portal): 'Không sử dụng hồ sơ bệnh án giấy từ ngày 01 tháng 01 năm 2027', relaying the text of Bộ Y tế Chỉ thị số 04/CT-BYT ngày 07/4/2026 về việc đẩy mạnh triển khai hồ sơ bệnh án điện tử
research.notes: Translation: 'In particular, hospitals (including public hospitals and private hospitals) are required not to use paper medical records from 1 January 2027.' Preceding sentence of the same directive, item 3: 'Các cơ sở khám bệnh, chữa bệnh rà soát, đánh giá hiện trạng, xây dựng kế hoạch triển khai cụ thể, huy động và bổ sung các nguồn lực để bảo đảm việc hoàn thành triển khai hồ sơ bệnh án điện tử tại đơn vị chậm nhất vào ngày 31 tháng 12 năm 2026.' (all examination and treatment facilities must complete electronic medical records by 31 December 2026). The directive cites Thông tư 13/2025/TT-BYT (6 Jun 2025, in force 21 Jul 2025), whose roadmap set 30/9/2025 for hospitals and 31/12/2026 for other facilities (government portal summary, https://xaydungchinhsach.chinhphu.vn/lo-trinh-trien-khai-ho-so-benh-an-dien-tu-tai-cac-benh-vien-119250610163849953.htm, 13 Jun 2025, read through a summarising fetch). Second source, VnEconomy 11 Mar 2026, https://vneconomy.vn/cac-benh-vien-khong-su-dung-benh-an-giay-tu-112027.htm , on the MoH 2026 plan (Quyết định 965/QĐ-BYT, 10 Apr 2026): 'Trong đó, tất cả các bệnh viện (bao gồm bệnh viện công lập, bệnh viện tư nhân) không sử dụng hồ sơ bệnh án giấy từ ngày 1/1/2027.' and 'Bộ Y tế đặt mục tiêu bảo đảm 100% các cơ sở khám bệnh, chữa bệnh trên toàn quốc hoàn thành triển khai hồ sơ bệnh án điện tử vào 31/12/2026.' Kind of private: bệnh viện tư nhân (privately owned hospitals), which in Vietnam treat both social-health-insurance and self-pay patients; the rule names the institutions, not the payer, and does not yet name private clinics (phòng khám tư nhân) separately, though 'các cơ sở khám bệnh, chữa bệnh' covers them with the 31/12/2026 date. Write vs read: the directive concerns electronic medical records inside each facility, which is the precondition for feeding the shared record; the shared record itself is Sổ sức khỏe điện tử on VNeID and the national health database under Nghị định 102/2025/NĐ-CP (in force 1 Jul 2025), and the Ministry of Health states that it applies to public and private facilities alike: VOV2 (state broadcaster), 6 Jan 2026, https://vov2.vov.vn/suc-khoe/so-suc-khoe-dien-tu-tren-vneid-chinh-thuc-thay-the-so-giay-56670.vov2 : 'Sổ sức khoẻ điện tử VNeID được sử dụng cho tất cả các cơ sở khám, chữa bệnh công lập và tư nhân, cả loại hình khám chữa bệnh ngoại trú, nội trú, khám chữa bệnh từ xa'. Gap: the ministry's own count was 1,268 of 1,650 public and private hospitals running electronic records on 19 Sep 2026 (existing country file; the moh.gov.vn page timed out, a provincial CDC mirror dated 14 Sep 2026 gives 1,265 facilities on the MoH EMR portal). The 99.5% link to Vietnam Social Security eligibility checking is an insurer link and is not counted. Rule in force names private hospitals with a future deadline (1 Jan 2027) and the ministry names an incomplete count, so partial. Existing country file class: unknown; this research gives partial.

research.quote: The urgency of this action cannot be overstated, as failing to integrate information systems across public and private sectors could lead to a fragmented foundation for the NHI, undermining its effectiveness and efficiency.
research.source: National Department of Health (Republic of South Africa), 2nd Presidential Health Compact 2024-2029: Accelerating Health System Strengthening and National Health Insurance (NHI) Implementation (Pillar 9 chapter)
research.notes: English source, no translation needed. Kind of private: the whole private sector (private hospital groups, private GPs and specialists paid by medical schemes or out of pocket), which the Compact treats as a separate sector whose information systems are yet to be integrated with the public ones; the sentence precedes the Compact's call for Section 74 National Health Act regulations and its 2024-2029 target to build a 'Shared Electronic Health Record system' with 'Private Sector' listed only as a supporting party. Write vs read: there is no shared record for anyone to write to yet; the only national platform is the Health Patient Registration System (HPRS), a demographic registration system, not a clinical record. Same source, same chapter, current-state bullets: 'A notable gap in comprehensive patient registers affects both the public and private sectors' and 'The non-availability of essential patient health records at the point of care is due to fragmented patient information systems'. Second source: National Department of Health Annual Report 2024/2025 (gov.za, published 2025-11), https://www.gov.za/sites/default/files/gcis_document/202511/department-health-annual-report-2024-2025.pdf : 'The scoping exercise for the Single Patient Viewer (SPV) as the forerunner to the longitudinal patient record and the shared electronic health record has been completed.' and 'As of the end of 2024/25, it [HPRS] has been implemented in 3 265 public health facilities and holds over 68 million individual records' (elsewhere: '3 266 health establishments (3150 fixed PHC facilities, 113 hospitals and three General Practitioner practices)', the three GP practices being the only non-public sites named). Third source: L Prinsen, PER/PELJ 2026(29), published 2026-03-20, https://perjournal.co.za/article/download/21166/25515 : 'In South Africa, a developing nation, the use of EHRs is considered a relatively new development in the private sector while paper records are still predominantly used in the public health sector.' Law: NHI Act 20 of 2023 (assented 2024-05-16) s 39(2)(v) would make 'submission of information to the national health information system to ensure portability and continuity of health care services' a condition of provider accreditation, but the Act is NOT in force: no section has been proclaimed, and SAnews (2026-02-24, https://www.sanews.gov.za/south-africa/president-delays-proclamation-sections-nhi-act) reports the President 'agree[d] to delay the proclamation of any sections of the National Health Insurance (NHI) Act until the Constitutional Court has handed down its judgments'. National Health Act s 74 (2003) only mandates NDoH to coordinate private-sector information systems into a national health information system; the Compact says the regulations to do so are still being urged. Caveat on the quote: it is phrased as a warning about a pending action (integration across public and private sectors has not happened), not as a flat 'records are not linked' statement; no source found says any private provider writes to a public record, and the public shared EHR itself is at scoping stage. The Health Market Inquiry final report (2019) was opened and has no usable sentence on records. Agrees with the existing country-file class (split: 'Public and private care run separate systems.').
